Among the grades listed here that ordering places Outstanding first, then grade A, then Pass, then Fail, then Absent. questions.text: Which of the following, taken together, make a valid syllogism? A. Apples are not sweets. B. Some apples are sweets. C. All sweets are tasty. D. Some apples are not tasty. E. No apple is tasty. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.expl: Take 'All sweets are tasty' (C) and 'No apple is tasty' (E). If any apple were a sweet it would have to be tasty, contradicting E; hence no apple is a sweet, i.e. 'Apples are not sweets' (A). So C and E validly yield A. The other groupings mix particular and negative premises that do not produce a valid conclusion.

questions.text: Arrange the following in a meaningful order, from particular to general: A. Family B. Community C. Member D. Locality E. Country Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.expl: Moving from the most specific unit outward: a Member belongs to a Family, families form a Community, communities occupy a Locality, and localities together make up a Country — C, A, B, D, E.

questions.text: Arrange the following computers in chronological order: A. The Atanasoff Berry Computer (ABC) B. IBM-701 C. The Mark I Computer D. UNIVAC I E. IBM-650 Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.expl: The correct history is ABC (1942) → Mark I (1944) → UNIVAC I (1951) → IBM 701 (1952) → IBM 650 (1953–54), i.e. A, C, D, B, E. The printed options 1–3 did not contain this sequence, so option D has been editorially corrected to 'A, C, D, B, E' and is the intended key.

questions.text: Which of the following are used as Social Networking Sites? A. Twitter B. Instagram C. LinkedIn D. Blackbox E. Snapchat Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.expl: Twitter, Instagram, LinkedIn and Snapchat are all social-networking platforms. 'Blackbox' is not a social network (the term refers to opaque systems / flight recorders), so the correct set is A, B, C, E.

questions.text: Select the characteristics of the Learner-Centred Approach. A. It is centred on the needs of the learner predecided by her parents. B. It lays emphasis on skills. C. It lays emphasis on indirect strategies. D. It is dependent on the training the teacher has gone through. E. It can be used in privately managed schools only. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, D and E only
questions.expl: A learner-centred approach builds on the learner's own needs and interests, emphasises skills and competencies (B) and uses indirect, facilitative strategies (C). It is not dictated by parents (A) or limited by teacher training (D), and it is not restricted to private schools (E).

questions.text: Working of the circulatory system of the human body is shown by a teacher on a screen. Such simulations have tremendous potential for instructional purposes. This aligns best with:
questions.expl: Using a screen-based simulation to demonstrate a process is a textbook case of computer-aided learning, where the computer delivers or models the content. Activity-based and heuristic learning need the learner's own hands-on inquiry, and peer-tutoring involves students teaching each other.

questions.text: The NPE 1986 envisaged setting up residential schools with the aim of providing excellence coupled with equity and social justice. This led to the establishment of:
questions.expl: Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas were created under the National Policy on Education 1986 as pace-setting residential schools for talented rural children, combining excellence with equity. Kendriya Vidyalayas predate 1986 and serve transferable central employees; Eklavya schools are for tribal students under a later scheme.

questions.text: A term drawn from theology, concerned with the theory and method of the interpretation of human action, is known as:
questions.expl: Hermeneutics originated as the discipline of interpreting scripture and was extended to the interpretation of texts and human action generally; it is a key interpretive paradigm in qualitative research. Grounded theory is a method of building theory from data, not an interpretive tradition.

questions.text: Select the correct number sequences from the following: A. 5, 7, 13, 25, 45, 75 B. 17, 40, 109, 224, 385 C. 4, 11, 19, 41, 79, 169 D. 3, 2, 0, -9, -52, -280 E. 4, 13, 31, 67, 139, 280 Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.expl: Series A has first differences 2, 6, 12, 20, 30 whose second differences are a constant 2, so it follows a consistent rule. Series B has first differences 23, 69, 115, 161 with a constant second difference of 46. Series C, D and E break their own patterns, so only A and B are consistent sequences.

questions.text: Select the correct statements in the context of communication models. A. Feedback is the transmission of the receiver's reaction back to the sender. B. Encoding is the task/process done at the receiver's end. C. Noise is anything added to the signal between transmission and reception that is not intended by the source. D. Decoding is the task/process done at the sender's end. E. Medium is the means through which the message is conveyed. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.expl: Feedback is the receiver's response sent back to the sender (A, true), noise is unintended interference added in the channel (C, true) and the medium carries the message (E, true). Encoding is done by the sender and decoding by the receiver, so B and D are false. The correct set A, C & E was not among the printed choices, so option D has been editorially corrected to 'A, C & E only' and is the intended key.

questions.text: The ability to access, analyze, evaluate and communicate media messages is:
questions.expl: Media literacy is standardly defined as the ability to access, analyse, evaluate and create/communicate messages across media. Propaganda and media hype are types of persuasive content, not a competency.

questions.expl: Reducing the computer price by seventeen percent leaves eighty-three percent of fifty thousand, which is forty-one thousand five hundred rupees. Since the person spends fifty thousand rupees altogether, the amount left for the printer is fifty thousand minus forty-one thousand five hundred, that is eight thousand five hundred rupees. The printer originally cost twenty thousand, so the reduction is eleven thousand fiv

questions.text: Arrange the following steps in the process of deduction: A. Theory B. Hypothesis C. Data collection D. Revision of theory E. Findings Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.expl: Deductive research starts from an existing Theory, derives a testable Hypothesis, then moves to Data collection, produces Findings, and finally leads to Revision of the theory — A, B, C, E, D.

questions.text: Select the correct statements pertaining to NEP 2020. A. It promotes secular and minorities education vehemently. B. It promotes multiple-entry–multiple-exit in higher education. C. It recommends that the state must spend 10 percent of GDP on education. D. It affirms that Sanskrit has more literature than Latin and Persian. E. It promotes private philanthropic education. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.expl: NEP 2020 introduces multiple entry and exit points in higher education (B), states that Sanskrit literature is larger than that of Latin and Greek/Persian (D), and encourages private philanthropic participation in education (E). It recommends 6% of GDP (not 10%), so C is wrong, and it does not frame itself in the terms of statement A.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. Choose the correct answer from the options: List-I (Broken Rule) List-II (Associated Fallacy) A. Middle term undistributed in the premises. B. Presence of two negative premises in an argument. C. Particular conclusion with negative premises. D. Any term distributed in the conclusion but undistributed in the premises. I. Existential Fallacy II. Fallacy of illicit major and minor term III. Exclusive premises IV. Undistributed Middle
questions.expl: An undistributed middle term is the fallacy of Undistributed Middle (IV). Two negative premises is the fallacy of Exclusive Premises (III). Drawing a particular conclusion where the premise structure does not support existence is the Existential Fallacy (I). A term distributed in the conclusion but not in the premises is the fallacy of illicit major/minor term (II). Hence A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: SSD stands for:
questions.expl: SSD stands for Solid State Disk (also called Solid State Drive) — storage built from flash memory with no moving parts, unlike a magnetic hard disk.

questions.text: Planning teaching involves making decisions. Which of the following decisions reflects this dictum?
options: Selection of the course for admission
questions.expl: Instructional planning is about decisions internal to teaching — what content to teach and which methods and materials to use. Choosing a profession, a course, or migration are personal career decisions, not part of planning a lesson.

questions.text: Per- and Polyfluorinated alkyl substances are called 'Forever Chemicals' because they are highly persistent. They can be found in: A. Paper and cardboard food packaging B. Textiles C. DDT D. Cosmetics E. Nuclear industry waste Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.expl: PFAS are used for their water- and grease-repellent properties in food packaging (A), stain-resistant textiles (B) and cosmetics (D). DDT is an organochlorine pesticide, and nuclear waste is a radiological problem — neither is a PFAS source.

questions.text: Arrange the following chronologically: A. University of Bombay, Calcutta and Madras B. University Grants Commission C. Panjab University, Lahore D. Banaras Hindu University E. University of Delhi Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.expl: The three presidency universities were founded in 1857, Panjab University in 1882, Banaras Hindu University in 1916, the University of Delhi in 1922, and the UGC was set up in 1953 (statutory 1956) — order A, C, D, E, B.

questions.expl: Maslow's pyramid rises Physiological → Safety → Belongingness and love → Esteem → Self-actualization, which maps to B, D, C, E, A.

questions.expl: Tom Hanks starred in Forrest Gump (II), Guru Dutt in Pyaasa (III), Tom Cruise in the Mission: Impossible series (IV), and Leonardo DiCaprio in Titanic (I) — A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questions.text: Arrange the following industrial sources of noise in descending order of their noise level (in dB): A. Steel plate riveting B. High-speed drill C. Circular saw D. Farm tractor E. Milling machine Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.expl: By typical measured sound-pressure levels the loudest is the high-speed drill, followed by steel plate riveting, the farm tractor, the circular saw and then the milling machine — B, A, D, C, E.

'A break in the chronology of a narrative in which events from the past are disclosed to the reader, listener or viewer and which have a bearing on the present situation' can be easily noticed in cinema. What is this style called?
questions.expl: Interrupting the present narrative to show earlier events that bear on the current situation is a flashback. A flash-forward does the opposite — it jumps ahead to future events.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. Choose the correct answer from the options: List-I (Fuel Alcohol) List-II (Characteristic) A. Methanol B. Ethanol C. Gasohol D. Butanol I. Mixture of ethanol and gasoline II. High energy content III. Produced by bacterial anaerobic digestion IV. Can be derived from potato waste
questions.expl: Methanol has a high energy content relative to other fuel alcohols (II), ethanol can be produced from potato waste and other biomass (IV), gasohol is a blend of ethanol and gasoline (I), and butanol can be obtained by bacterial anaerobic digestion (III) — A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. Choose the correct answer from the options: List-I (Scheme / Institution) List-II (Function) A. Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan B. e-Pathshala C. NAS D. NTSE I. Identification of talented students II. Assessment of learning outcomes III. To promote scientific temper and innovation IV. Digital access to textbooks and resources
questions.expl: Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan promotes scientific temper and innovation (III), e-Pathshala provides digital access to textbooks and resources (IV), the National Achievement Survey assesses learning outcomes (II), and the NTSE identifies talented students (I) — A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. Choose the correct answer from the options: List-I (Approach of Scale Construction) List-II (Process Followed) A. Arbitrary approach B. Factor Scales C. Consensus approach D. Cumulative Scales I. A panel evaluates the items chosen for inclusion in the instrument according to their relevance II. Scale is developed on an ad hoc basis III. Intercorrelation of items which indicates that a common factor accounts for the relationship between items IV. Chosen on the basis of their conforming to some ranking of items with ascending or descending discriminating power
questions.expl: In the arbitrary approach the scale is built on an ad hoc basis (II). Factor scales are derived from the intercorrelation of items reflecting a common factor (III). In the consensus approach a panel judges the relevance of items for inclusion (I). Cumulative (Guttman-type) scales order items by ascending or descending discriminating power (IV) — A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV.

questions.text: E-learning strategies are supported by: A. Virtual Classroom B. TCP/IP C. Instant messaging D. Satellite classroom E. Web casting Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.expl: Virtual classrooms, instant messaging and web casting are instructional strategies for delivering e-learning. TCP/IP is the underlying network protocol (infrastructure, not a strategy) and a satellite classroom is a transmission arrangement rather than an e-learning strategy, so the answer is A, C, E only.

questions.text: Arrange the following United Nations conferences/conventions according to the year they were held: A. The Stockholm Conference B. The Kyoto Protocol C. The Montreal Protocol D. The Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer E. The Convention on Biological Diversity Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.expl: Chronology: Stockholm Conference (1972), Vienna Convention (1985), Montreal Protocol (1987), Convention on Biological Diversity (1992) and Kyoto Protocol (1997) — A, D, C, E, B.

questions.text: Arrange the steps of research sequentially: A. Writing report B. Data analysis C. Review of literature D. Choice of research design E. Sampling and data collection Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.expl: A research study proceeds Review of literature → Choice of research design → Sampling and data collection → Data analysis → Writing report — C, D, E, B, A.

questions.text: The difference in sea-surface temperature between one location in the Western Indian Ocean and one location in the Eastern Indian Ocean is called:
questions.expl: The Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) is defined by the gradient in sea-surface temperature between the western and eastern tropical Indian Ocean. ENSO is a Pacific phenomenon and the Madden-Julian Oscillation is an eastward-moving tropical convection pulse.

questions.text: Which of the following Pramanas (valid means of knowledge) are accepted by the Nyaya school of philosophy?
options: Pratyaksha, Anumana, Verbal Testimony (Shabda) and Upamana
questions.expl: Nyaya accepts four pramanas: Pratyaksha (perception), Anumana (inference), Upamana (comparison) and Shabda (verbal testimony). Schools such as Charvaka accept only perception; the fuller list of six belongs to Advaita Vedanta.

questions.text: In the first figure, which are the valid moods? A. AAA B. AEE C. EAE D. AOO E. EIO Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.expl: The valid moods of the first figure are AAA (Barbara), EAE (Celarent), AII (Darii) and EIO (Ferio). From the given list that is A, C and E. AEE and AOO are not valid in the first figure.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. Choose the correct answer from the options: List-I (Teaching Model) List-II (Feature) A. Personal Basis Model B. Social Interaction Model C. Behaviour Altering Model D. Information Development Model I. Working in a group II. Teacher as the main figure in class III. Memorization, practice and transfer of learning IV. Instruction based on human relations
questions.expl: The Personal Basis (personal source) model is built on human relations and the learner's self (IV). The Social Interaction model centres on working in a group (I). Behaviour-altering models place the teacher/environment as the controlling figure that shapes responses (II). Information-development (information-processing) models stress memorization, practice and transfer of learning (III) — A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

questions.text: Which of the following are methods of control of intervening variables? A. Deductive manipulation B. Inferential manipulation C. Statistical manipulation D. Physical manipulation E. Selective manipulation Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.expl: Extraneous or intervening variables are controlled by physical manipulation (holding conditions constant / randomisation), selective manipulation (choosing or matching cases) and statistical manipulation (partialling out effects through analysis). 'Deductive' and 'inferential' manipulation are not recognised control techniques, so the answer is C, D, E only.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. Choose the correct answer from the options: List-I (Concept) List-II (Feature) A. Algorithm B. Modem C. Bandwidth D. Flowchart I. Range of frequencies over which signals are transmitted II. Converts digital signals to sine waves and vice-versa III. Pictorial representation of a computational procedure IV. Finite sequence to solve a problem
questions.expl: An algorithm is a finite sequence of steps to solve a problem (IV). A modem converts digital signals to analog (sine) waves and back (II). Bandwidth is the range of frequencies over which signals are transmitted (I). A flowchart is a pictorial representation of a computational procedure (III) — A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III.

Oliver calls this the personal tragedy model because it tends to describe disability as some terrible personal problem, which has ruined that person's life. He suggests that this model has now become taken for granted, achieving 'ideological hegemony' in the way that disabled people are viewed. In place of the individualistic or perso
options: Giving adequate medical treatment to everyone.
Reorganizing society to facilitate access of all social space to the impaired.
Re-orienting parents to prevent the birth of disabled children.
questions.expl: Oliver's social model holds that disability is produced when society is organised so that impaired people cannot use social spaces; therefore removing those barriers — ramps, lower counters, adequate space — removes the disability. Medical treatment (A) and 're-orienting' disabled persons or parents (C, D) target the individual, which is exactly the personal-tragedy view Oliver rejects.

He suggests that this model has now become taken for granted, achieving 'ideological hegemony' in the way that disabled people are viewed. In place of the indiv
options: It is an accident that makes one impaired, not a wilful choice.
In society, disability is a taboo.
It sees disability as an individualistic problem that disrupts one's life.
It is not the willingness of God to make someone disabled.
questions.expl: The passage says the personal tragedy model 'tends to describe disability as some terrible personal problem, which has ruined that person's life' and stresses that the individual must cope alone. Oliver objects precisely to this individualistic framing; the other options are not the reason given in the text.

Oliver calls this the personal tragedy model because it tends to describe disability as some terrible personal problem, which has ruined that person's life. questions.expl: Oliver draws the line between a bodily impairment a person has and the disability that society creates when it organises social and economic life so as to translate that impairment into exclusion. So impairment is personal/bodily while disability is socially produced.

Individual as a part of society has gone through personal tragedy.
Impairment and disability are one and the same.
questions.expl: Oliver insists disability 'can only be understood within a wider social and economic framework' — it is the way society organises social and economic features that converts an impairment into a disability. Option C restates the personal-tragedy view he rejects, and option D denies the impairment/disability distinction he insists on.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II A. Pivot point B. Fixed point C. Mirror image D. Distortion I. Reflection II. Shear III. Rotation IV. Scaling
questions.expl: A pivot point remains fixed during rotation, a fixed point is associated with scaling, a mirror image is produced by reflection, and shear produces distortion. Therefore the matching is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: How many edges are there in a graph with 10 vertices, each of degree six?
questions.expl: By the handshaking lemma, the sum of degrees equals twice the number of edges. The degree sum is 10 × 6 = 60, so the graph has 60/2 = 30 edges. Taking 60 itself would confuse the degree sum with the edge count.

questions.text: Which of the following have true value when the universe of discourse is all integers? A. ∃n (2n = 3n) B. ∃n (n² > n) C. ∀n (2n > n) D. ∃n (n² = 2) E. ∀x∀y ∃z (xy = z)
options: A, B, C and D only
B, C, D and E only
questions.expl: A is true at n = 0, and B is true, for example at n = 2. C fails at negative integers, D is false because √2 is not an integer, and E is true because the product of any two integers is an integer. Hence A, B and E are true.

questions.text: Arrange the following in the correct order in the context of the OSI model, from bottom to top. A. Network layer B. Physical layer C. Presentation layer D. Data link layer E. Application layer
questions.expl: The OSI stack rises from Physical to Data Link to Network to Presentation to Application. Replacing these with the supplied letters gives B, D, A, C, E.

questions.text: Which topology requires a central controller or a hub?
questions.expl: A star topology connects every device to a central hub or switch. Bus and ring topologies use a shared backbone or loop, while a mesh uses multiple direct links.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II A. Wait-for graph B. Precedence graph C. Rigorous 2PL D. Strict 2PL I. Holds all locks until it commits II. Holds write-locks until it commits III. Used to check deadlocks IV. Used to check serializability
questions.expl: A wait-for graph is used to detect deadlocks, and a precedence graph is used to test serializability. Rigorous 2PL retains all locks until commit, whereas strict 2PL retains write locks until commit.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: SMTP response code List-II: Description A. 214 B. 421 C. 220 D. 554 I. Service ready II. Transaction failed III. Help message IV. Service not available
questions.expl: SMTP code 214 is a help message, 421 means service not available, 220 means service ready, and 554 indicates a transaction failed. These pairings produce A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statements about protocols used in the TCP/IP protocol suite. A. IP is a reliable connectionless protocol. B. ARP finds a node's physical address from its logical address. C. ICMP sends notification of datagram problems to the recipient of the message. D. IGMP facilitates simultaneous transmission of a message to a group of recipients.
questions.expl: IP is connectionless but does not provide reliable delivery, so A is incorrect. ICMP reports errors to the sender/source, not the recipient, so C is incorrect. ARP and IGMP are correctly described.

questions.text: Which technology enables the creation of virtual servers in a cloud-computing environment?
questions.expl: A hypervisor abstracts physical hardware so that several isolated virtual machines can run on a host. DNS, firewalls, and load balancers serve different network or traffic-management roles.

questions.text: Which document outlines the functional and non-functional requirements of a software system?
questions.expl: A Software Requirements Specification defines what the system must do and the quality constraints it must meet. Design documents describe implementation choices, while test plans and manuals serve later purposes.

questions.text: What does Amdahl's Law describe in the context of parallel processing?
options: Maximum speedup achievable, considering serial and parallel portions of a program
Efficiency of message passing in a distributed-memory system
Computational efficiency of a parallel algorithm
questions.expl: Amdahl's Law bounds the speedup obtainable by parallelisation using the fraction that remains serial. Even infinitely fast parallel work cannot remove the serial bottleneck.

questions.text: Arrange the following in terms of capacity from smallest to largest. A. L3 cache B. L1 cache C. CPU register D. L2 cache
questions.expl: Registers are the smallest storage locations, followed by L1 cache, then L2 cache, and then the larger L3 cache. Thus the increasing-capacity sequence is C, B, D, A.

questions.text: Let ⟨H₁, *⟩ and ⟨H₂, *⟩ be subgroups of the group ⟨G, *⟩. Which statement is false?
options: H₁H₂ = {h₁ * h₂ : h₁ ∈ H₁ and h₂ ∈ H₂} is a subgroup.
H₁H₂ is a normal subgroup when H₁ and H₂ are normal subgroups.
The set difference H₁ − H₂ is a subgroup.
questions.expl: The supplied source confirms option A as the false statement. The product set H₁H₂ need not be a subgroup unless additional conditions, such as normality of one factor, hold. Intersections of subgroups are always subgroups.

questions.text: Which field deals with interaction between computers and humans using natural language?
questions.expl: Natural Language Processing (NLP) is the AI field concerned with computer processing and generation of human language. PROLOG and LISP are programming languages, while ELIZA is an early NLP-style program rather than the name of the field.

questions.text: In rate-monotonic scheduling, a task has a period of 80 ms and an execution time of 55 ms. What are its processor utilisation and task rate?
questions.expl: Utilisation is execution time divided by period: 55/80 = 0.6875, approximately 0.69. The task rate is 1/0.08 seconds = 12.5 Hz. The other rates do not correspond to an 80 ms period.

questions.text: What is the correct sequence of the database-design process? A. Create conceptual schema B. Data model mapping C. Requirements collection and analysis D. Physical design
questions.expl: Database design starts by collecting and analysing requirements. It then develops a conceptual schema, maps that conceptual model to the selected data model, and finally performs physical design. Therefore the order is C, A, B, D.

questions.text: Choose the correct bottom-to-top order in the OSI model. A. Transforming datagrams into frames for transmission B. Transmission of bits over a communication channel C. Handling the user interface D. Control and monitoring of the subnet E. Transmission using a connection-oriented or connectionless protocol
questions.expl: Physical-layer work is B, data-link framing is A, network-layer subnet control is D, transport-layer service is E, and user-facing handling is C. This gives B, A, D, E, C.

questions.text: Given Pred(x) = x − 1 and T(x, y + 1) = Pred(T(x, y)), with T(x, 0) = x, which operation is a candidate for T?
questions.expl: The recurrence applies the predecessor operation once for every increment of y. Thus T(x, y) = x − y, which is subtraction; addition would instead require a successor operation.

questions.text: For relation schema r(M, Y, P, MP, C), the functional dependencies are M → MP, {M, Y} → P, and MP → C. Which is a key?
questions.expl: From M, we obtain MP and then C, but not Y or P. Adding Y allows {M, Y} → P, so the closure of {M, Y} contains every attribute. Neither M nor MP supplies Y and P, making {M, Y} the key.

questions.text: Which item is a problem in piggybacking acknowledgement frames? A. There is no need to send separate acknowledgement frames. B. It requires more bandwidth. C. The data-link layer must decide how long to wait for a packet to which the acknowledgement can be attached. D. The number of acknowledgement frames decreases.
questions.expl: Piggybacking reduces separate acknowledgement frames and saves bandwidth, so A and D are benefits and B is false. Its drawback is deciding how long to delay an acknowledgement while waiting for outgoing data; that is C only.

questions.text: What is the maximum number of nodes that can be inserted in the AVL tree without changing its height? AVL tree with nodes 60, 50, 70, and 80.
questions.expl: The displayed tree has height 2 and currently contains 4 nodes. A binary tree of height 2 can contain at most 2³ − 1 = 7 nodes, so 7 − 4 = 3 additional nodes can be inserted without increasing its height.

questions.text: Each relation is defined on {1, 2, 3, 4}. Match List-I with List-II. List-I: Relation List-II: Relation type A. {(2,2), (2,3), (2,4), (3,2), (3,3), (3,4)} B. {(2,4), (4,2)} C. {(1,2), (2,3), (3,4)} D. {(1,3), (1,4), (2,3), (2,4), (3,1), (3,4)} I. Antisymmetric II. Only transitive III. Only symmetric IV. Neither symmetric nor transitive
questions.expl: A is transitive: its chained pairs such as (2,3) and (3,4) require (2,4), which is present, but it is not symmetric. B contains both (2,4) and (4,2), making it only symmetric. C has no reversed distinct pair, so it is antisymmetric, while D has neither property. Hence A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV is the required match.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II A. Macros B. Assembler C. Loader D. Compiler I. Converts high-level code to object (machine) code II. Used for code expansion III. Used to translate assembly-language code to object code IV. Used to allocate memory and relocate a program in memory
questions.expl: A macro is used for code expansion, an assembler translates assembly language to object code, a loader allocates memory and relocates a program, and a compiler translates high-level code. Therefore A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I is correct.

questions.text: How many solutions does x + y + z = 11 have, where x, y, and z are non-negative integers?
questions.expl: By stars and bars, the number of non-negative solutions to x + y + z = 11 is C(11 + 3 − 1, 3 − 1) = C(13, 2) = 78. This counts every allocation of 11 identical units among the three variables.

questions.text: Out of 32 people, 30 save paper and 14 save plastic bottles. If every person saves paper, plastic bottles, or both, how many save both?
questions.expl: Use inclusion–exclusion: |paper ∩ plastic| = |paper| + |plastic| − |paper ∪ plastic| = 30 + 14 − 32 = 12. Adding the two group totals without subtracting the overlap would double-count those 12 people.

questions.text: Arrange these language families from specialization to generalization. A. All regular languages B. All Turing-acceptable languages C. All Turing-decidable languages D. All context-free languages
questions.expl: Every regular language is context-free; every context-free language is decidable; and every decidable language is Turing-acceptable (recursively enumerable). The inclusions therefore grow as A, D, C, B.

questions.text: What is the maximum Hamming distance among all pairs of the following binary codes? Code Binary value C₁ 00000 C₂ 01011 C₃ 10101
questions.expl: C₁ and C₂ differ in three positions, C₁ and C₃ differ in three positions, while C₂ = 01011 and C₃ = 10101 differ in four positions. Thus the maximum pairwise Hamming distance is 4.

questions.text: Which is not a concern during the management of a software project?
questions.expl: The project-management concerns in this classification are information, time, and money. Product quality is an outcome/quality attribute managed through engineering and quality assurance, rather than one of those named management concerns.

questions.text: Which relational-algebra expression is equivalent to the SQL query SELECT X FROM B WHERE Y?
questions.expl: The WHERE predicate is applied first, so σᵧ selects from relation B. The SELECT list is then applied, so πₓ projects attribute X. Reversing that order can discard the attribute needed by the selection.

questions.text: Which of the following are true? A. A database may have only one primary key. B. Every key is a candidate key. C. There can be multiple candidate keys. D. There can be more than one superkey. E. Every candidate key is a primary key.
questions.expl: A relation design chooses one candidate key as its primary key, but may have several candidate keys and many superkeys. A superkey need not be minimal, so B is false; only the selected candidate key is primary, so E is false.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II A. Commutative law B. Distributive law C. De Morgan law D. Absorption law I. P ∧ (Q ∨ R) ≡ (P ∧ Q) ∨ (P ∧ R) II. P ∧ (P ∨ Q) ≡ P III. P ∧ Q ≡ Q ∧ P IV. ¬(P ∨ Q) ≡ ¬P ∧ ¬Q
questions.expl: Commutativity is P ∧ Q ≡ Q ∧ P (III). Distribution is P ∧ (Q ∨ R) ≡ (P ∧ Q) ∨ (P ∧ R) (I), De Morgan's law is ¬(P ∨ Q) ≡ ¬P ∧ ¬Q (IV), and absorption is P ∧ (P ∨ Q) ≡ P (II). Thus the apparently similar formulas in I and II must not be swapped: I expands a conjunction while II removes a redundant disjunction.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II A. Merge sort B. Binary search C. Quick sort D. Search in an unsorted array I. n² II. n log n III. n IV. log n
questions.expl: Merge sort has O(n log n) complexity, binary search has O(log n), quicksort has O(n²) in the worst case, and searching an unsorted array has O(n). This produces A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: For a context-free grammar G and string x, membership x ∈ L(G) can be decided in polynomial time.
If L is context-free, then its complement is also context-free.
The language {aⁿbᵐcᵖ : m, n, p ≥ 0, m ≠ n or m ≠ p} is not deterministic context-free.
The class of deterministic context-free languages is closed under intersection.
questions.expl: The supplied source confirms option B as the intended incorrect statement: context-free languages are not closed under complement. The paper designates B as the single answer for this MCQ.

questions.text: For sending input I₆ to the output line of an 8×1 multiplexer, which selection-line combination is required?
questions.expl: An 8-to-1 multiplexer uses three select bits to encode the input index in binary. Since 6 in binary is 110, the select lines S₂S₁S₀ must be 110; 111 would instead select I₇.

questions.text: Arrange these C++ data types in non-decreasing order of representation length. A. char B. int C. float D. double
questions.expl: A char uses the least storage, followed by int; float is normally smaller than double. Hence the non-decreasing order is char, int, float, double: A, B, C, D.

questions.text: The number of leaf nodes in a full 4-ary rooted tree with n nodes is:
questions.expl: If I is the number of internal nodes, a full 4-ary tree has n = 4I + 1. Its leaves are L = n − I = 3I + 1 = (3n + 1)/4. The other formulas do not satisfy this relation for a full 4-ary tree.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: Process model List-II: Characteristic A. Classical waterfall model B. Prototype model C. Evolutionary model D. Spiral model I. Risk analysis II. Large problem with incremental delivery III. Clear requirements IV. Requirements are not well understood
questions.expl: The classical waterfall model assumes clear requirements. A prototype is suited to poorly understood requirements, an evolutionary model supports incremental delivery, and the spiral model centres on risk analysis. Thus the matching is A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II A. Latency B. Delay C. Throughput D. Interrupt I. Number of tasks completed in a given time period II. Causes the current activity to be deferred III. Time elapsed before next activity starts IV. Time to complete a single task
questions.expl: Latency is the time to complete one task, delay is the time before the next activity starts, throughput is the number of tasks completed per time period, and an interrupt defers the current activity. This gives A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II A. long signed int B. double C. long double D. unsigned character I. %lf II. %Lf III. %c IV. %ld
questions.expl: A long signed int uses %ld, double uses %lf, long double uses %Lf, and an unsigned character is read or printed with %c. Hence the matching is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: Language List-II: Type A. L₁ = {aⁿbᵐ | n, m ≥ 0} B. L₂ = {aⁿbᵐ | n = m ≥ 0} C. L₃ = {aⁿbⁿcⁿdⁿeⁿ | n ≥ 1} D. L₄ = {aⁿbᵐcᵐdⁿe² | n, m ≥ 0} I. Unrestricted II. Context sensitive III. Regular IV. Context free
questions.expl: The supplied source annotation designates option B, A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II, as the intended key. The language definitions are retained exactly as printed so learners can compare the paper's classification convention with the formal language hierarchy.

questions.text: The term "double buffered" is used in which of the following?
questions.expl: Double buffering permits one buffer to be filled while another is consumed, helping asynchronous producer and consumer rates operate smoothly. It is not an addressing mode, and serial communication by itself does not define double buffering.

questions.text: To define the relationship between two entity sets, which operation can be used?
questions.expl: A relationship set is formally a subset of the Cartesian product of participating entity sets. Concatenation, addition, and union do not construct tuples across the two sets in this way.

questions.text: What is the output of this C program? #include <stdio.h> int main() { int i; for (i = 0; i++ < 10;) printf("%d", i++); return 0; }
questions.expl: Each loop test increments i once, and printf prints i before incrementing it again. The printed values are therefore 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9; the next condition sees 10 and terminates the loop.

questions.text: For disk tracks numbered 0–49, the head starts at 15 and requests arrive for 4, 40, 11, 35, 7, and 14. Order these algorithms by total head movement in ascending order, assuming initial movement toward higher-numbered tracks when required. A. FCFS B. LOOK C. SSTF D. SCAN
questions.expl: SSTF travels 47 tracks, LOOK travels 61, SCAN travels 79, and FCFS travels 135. Thus the ascending order is SSTF, LOOK, SCAN, FCFS: C, B, D, A.

questions.text: For the primal program max cᵀx subject to Ax ≤ b, which stated dual program is true?
options: min bᵀy subject to Aᵀy ≤ c, y ≥ 0
min bᵀy subject to Aᵀy ≥ c, y ≥ 0
min bᵀy subject to Aᵀy = c, y ≥ 0
max bᵀy subject to Aᵀy = c
questions.expl: The paper uses the equality-form dual: minimise bᵀy subject to Aᵀy = c and y ≥ 0. Under that convention, option C is the stated dual program.

questions.text: Choose the right sequence of stages for data transmission using CSMA/CD. A. If the channel is clear, the sender sends data. B. The sender senses the channel for activity. C. The sender waits for a random back-off time before retransmitting. D. Collision detection occurs if two devices transmit at the same time.
questions.expl: CSMA/CD first senses the medium, then transmits if it is idle. A collision may be detected during transmission, after which a random back-off precedes retransmission. This is B, A, D, C.

questions.text: Arrange these numbers in ascending order by the number of distinct prime factors. A. 729 B. 1001 C. 1111 D. 420
questions.expl: Factor each number and count unique primes, not repeated powers: 729 = 3⁶ has 1; 1111 = 11 × 101 has 2; 1001 = 7 × 11 × 13 has 3; and 420 = 2² × 3 × 5 × 7 has 4. Sorting those counts from 1 to 4 gives A, C, B, D.

questions.text: A problem of size n requires n² bit operations. What is the largest instance that can be solved in one second if each bit operation takes 10⁻⁹ second?
questions.expl: One second permits 10⁹ operations. Solving n² = 10⁹ gives n = √10⁹ ≈ 3.16 × 10⁴. The larger choices confuse the operation budget with the square root of that budget.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II A. Disk scheduling B. Batch processing C. Time sharing D. Interrupt processing I. Round robin II. SCAN III. LIFO IV. FIFO
questions.expl: Disk scheduling uses SCAN, batch processing is handled in FIFO order, time sharing uses round robin, and interrupt processing uses LIFO nesting. Therefore the match is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

questions.text: Classifying email as spam, labeling web pages by context, and voice recognition are examples of which approach?
questions.expl: These tasks learn from examples with known labels, such as spam/not spam or a known spoken word. That is supervised learning; unsupervised learning has no target labels, while reinforcement learning optimises rewards through interaction.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. A. Stack B. Queue C. Linked list D. Binary search tree List-I List-II A. Stack B. Queue C. Linked list D. Binary search tree I. FIFO II. LIFO III. Ordered children IV. Sequentially linked dynamic nodes
questions.expl: A stack follows LIFO (II), a queue follows FIFO (I), a linked list has dynamically sized sequentially linked nodes (IV), and a binary search tree has ordered child nodes (III). Hence A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

questions.text: The combination of selection lines for sending input I₁₄ to the output in the shown 64 × 1 multiplexer is: 64 × 1 multiplexer selection-line diagram.
questions.expl: A 64-to-1 multiplexer needs six selection bits. The binary representation of input index 14 is 001110, so S₅…S₀ must be 001110; the other choices represent input indices 15, 48, and 60.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II A. SMTP I. Network layer B. UDP II. Transport layer C. Ethernet III. Application layer D. IP IV. Data-link layer
questions.expl: SMTP is an application-layer protocol, UDP is transport-layer, Ethernet is data-link-layer, and IP is network-layer. Thus the match is A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I.

questions.text: For the shown neural network, what are the net input yᵢₙ and final threshold output y? Neural-network inputs, weights, bias, and threshold function.
questions.expl: Using the diagram values, yᵢₙ = (0.5×0.5) + (0.6×−0.8) + (0.8×1) + 0.5 = 1.07. Since the threshold function returns 1 for an input at least 1, y = 1; the alternatives use an incorrect sign, omit a term, or put the total below the threshold.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. A. FDM B. Digital circuits C. A two-variable function D. J-K flip-flop List-I List-II A. FDM B. Digital circuits C. Two-variable function D. J-K flip-flop I. Four minterms II. Frequency Division Multiplexing III. Universal flip-flop IV. Combinational or sequential
questions.expl: FDM means frequency-division multiplexing (II). Digital circuits may be combinational or sequential (IV), a two-variable Boolean function has four minterms (I), and the J-K flip-flop is universal (III).

questions.text: The number of pixel columns divided by the number of scan lines displayed by a system is called:
questions.expl: Aspect ratio is the ratio of horizontal pixels (or columns) to vertical scan lines. A bitmap/pixmap is an image representation, while depth refers to bits per pixel.

questions.text: Which is not part of the general activation record of a procedure?
questions.expl: An activation record stores data associated with one invocation: local variables, temporary values, and links for non-local access. Global data has program-wide lifetime and is not stored in each procedure activation record.

questions.text: The number of vertices of odd degree in any graph is:
questions.expl: By the handshaking lemma, the sum of all vertex degrees equals 2e and is even. An even sum can contain only an even number of odd summands, so odd-degree vertices occur in pairs.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. A. Waterfall model B. Agile methodology C. Test-driven development D. Continuous integration List-I List-II A. Waterfall B. Agile C. TDD D. CI I. Collaboration/release feedback II. Automated integration III. Fixed sequential steps IV. Tests before code
questions.expl: Waterfall is sequential fixed stages (III), Agile uses iterative collaboration and feedback (I), TDD writes tests before implementation (IV), and continuous integration uses frequent integration and automated testing (II).

questions.text: In the worst case, the smallest number of comparisons required by a comparison-based sorting algorithm is:
questions.expl: A comparison sort must distinguish among n! possible input orders. Its decision tree therefore needs at least n! leaves, so its worst-case height is at least ⌈log₂(n!)⌉ comparisons.

questions.text: A single bit travels at 3 × 10⁸ m/s through a 12,000 km fibre-optic cable. What is its one-way propagation delay?
questions.expl: Convert 12,000 km to 1.2 × 10⁷ m. Divide distance by the stated speed: (1.2 × 10⁷)/(3 × 10⁸) = 0.04 seconds. Multiplying by 1,000 converts this to 40 ms, so option D is correct; 20 ms and 5 ms result from incorrect unit conversion or arithmetic.

questions.text: Which statements about UDP are true? A. It is called Uniform Data Protocol. B. It is called User Datagram Protocol. C. It belongs to the Transport layer. D. It belongs to the Network layer.
questions.expl: UDP expands to User Datagram Protocol and operates at the transport layer. IP is a network-layer protocol; “Uniform Data Protocol” is not UDP’s expansion.

questions.text: Match the equivalent propositions in List-I and List-II. List-I List-II A. P → (Q → P) B. P → (Q ∨ R) C. (P → Q) ∧ (R → Q) D. ¬(P ⇔ Q) I. (P ∨ Q) ∧ ¬(P ∧ Q) II. (P ∨ R) → Q III. (P → Q) ∨ (P → R) IV. ¬P → (P → Q)
questions.expl: For A, Q → P is ¬Q ∨ P, so P → (Q → P) is ¬P ∨ ¬Q ∨ P, a tautology; IV is also a tautology. For B, P → (Q ∨ R) becomes ¬P ∨ Q ∨ R, exactly III. Applying (X→Q) = ¬X∨Q to C gives (¬P∨Q)∧(¬R∨Q) = ¬(P∨R)∨Q, which is II. Finally ¬(P⇔Q) is true exactly when one, but not both, of P and Q is true, which is I.

questions.text: Which is not a characteristic of linked-list file allocation?
options: No space is lost to external disk fragmentation, apart from possible internal fragmentation in the final block
Reading files or random access is very fast
The data portion of a block is reduced because a pointer occupies some bytes
The disadvantages can be mitigated with a main-memory File Allocation Table (FAT)
questions.expl: Linked allocation follows pointers one block at a time, so direct/random access is slow. It avoids external fragmentation, reserves pointer space in each block, and FAT can retain the links in memory to improve traversal.

questions.text: A safe expression in relational calculus is guaranteed to yield:
options: A finite number of null values
questions.expl: Safety (range restriction) ensures that query variables range over values drawn from the finite database domain. This prevents an expression from describing infinitely many result tuples.

questions.text: A doctor knows P(s | m) = 0.70, P(m) = 1/50,000, and P(s) = 0.01, where s is a stiff neck and m is meningitis. Compute P(m | s).
questions.expl: Bayes’ rule gives P(m | s) = P(s | m)P(m)/P(s) = 0.70 × (1/50,000) / 0.01 = 0.0014. The disease remains unlikely even after observing the symptom because its prior probability is very small.

questions.text: Let P denote power set and ∅ the empty set. Arrange in non-decreasing cardinality: A. P({a,b,{a,b }}) B. P({∅,a,{a},{{a }}}) C. P(P(∅)) D. P(P({a})) E. P({{a,b},c})
questions.expl: P(∅) has one member, so C = P(P(∅)) has 2 members. P({a}) has 2 members, so D has 4; E also has two underlying elements and has 4. A has three underlying elements and therefore 8 members, while B has four and therefore 16. Thus C, D, E, A, B is the listed non-decreasing order.

questions.text: What is the height of the binary search tree formed by inserting 40, 60, 50, 37, 52, 15, 8, 22 in that order?
questions.expl: The longest root-to-leaf path is 40 → 37 → 15 → 8 (or 40 → 60 → 50 → 52). It has three edges, so under the usual edge-height definition the tree height is 3.

Using the paper's stated composition convention, the resulting relation is {(1,5),(3,2),(2,5)}, which is option B. This convention fixes the order in which the two relation mappings are composed for this question.

questions.text: Which option is the minimized DFA equivalent to the DFA shown? Original DFA and the four proposed minimized automata.
questions.expl: The accepting state q4 is distinct. The remaining non-accepting states partition into two equivalent behaviours, producing the three-state DFA shown in option 1: an initial state A, state B with a 0 loop, and accepting state C reached on 1.

questions.text: For the reference string 7,0,1,2,0,3,0,4,2,3,0,3,2,1,2,0,1,7,0,1 with three frames, what is the hit ratio under optimal page replacement?
questions.expl: Simulating OPT gives 11 hits in the 20 references. On each miss with full frames, OPT replaces the resident page whose next use is farthest in the future (or never occurs again), so the hit ratio is 11/20.

questions.text: Average main-memory access time is 130 ns, cache access time is 100 ns, and the cache hit ratio is 75%. What is the average time to access a word?
questions.expl: Separate the accesses into 75 cache hits and 25 misses per 100 references. Those contribute 75 × 100 ns and 25 × 130 ns respectively, totalling 10,750 ns; dividing by 100 gives 107.5 ns. The other answers omit the hit ratio or reverse the two access times.

questions.text: Which IC family has the lowest power consumption?
questions.expl: CMOS has very low static power consumption because its complementary transistor pair ideally draws significant current only while switching. ECL and TTL consume substantially more steady power.

questions.text: How will the shown min-heap appear after inserting key 32? Original min-heap and the four candidate heaps after insertion.
questions.expl: The new key is first placed at the next open leaf, as the left child of 40. Since 32 < 40, it swaps once with 40; it then stops because 32 > its new parent 10. This is exactly the heap shown in option 3.

questions.text: What is the maximum bit rate of a noiseless channel with bandwidth 2 kHz transmitting a signal with 8 levels?
questions.expl: By the Nyquist formula, maximum bit rate = 2B log₂L = 2 × 2000 × log₂8 = 4000 × 3 = 12,000 bps. Using 8 directly rather than log₂8 produces the larger distractors.

questions.text: Which of the following is not an interprocess communication mechanism in UNIX?
questions.expl: Pipes, message queues, and shared memory transfer information between processes. A semaphore is principally a synchronization primitive: it coordinates access rather than carrying a message payload.

questions.text: Which statements about C++ constructors are correct? A. They have the same name as the class. B. They can return values. C. They are called automatically when an object is created. D. They can be overloaded. E. They can be inherited.
options: A, B, C and D only
questions.expl: A constructor is named for its class, is invoked on object creation, and may be overloaded. It has no return type or return value, and constructors are not inherited, so A, C, and D are the correct statements.

questions.text: A tree is: A. a circuitless connected graph B. a connected graph of n vertices with (n − 1) edges C. a circuitless graph of n vertices with (n − 1) edges D. a minimally connected graph
questions.expl: These are equivalent characterisations of a finite tree. A connected acyclic graph has n − 1 edges; an acyclic graph with n − 1 edges is connected; and every edge is necessary for connectivity, which is minimal connectedness.

questions.text: If f(n) = θ(g(n)) and g(n) = O(h(n)), which statement is true?
questions.expl: f(n) = θ(g(n)) implies f(n) = O(g(n)). Combining this with g(n) = O(h(n)) and transitivity of big-O gives f(n) = O(h(n)). The information does not establish a reverse bound, so the theta claims need not hold.

questions.text: What is z after this C code executes? x = 16; y = 4; z = x >> y;
questions.expl: Right shifting a positive integer by four places divides it by 2⁴. Thus 16 >> 4 equals 16 / 16 = 1; the other answers correspond to fewer shifts or a different operation.

questions.text: Simplify F(A,B,C,D) = Σm(3,6,7,11,12,13,14,15) using a four-variable Karnaugh map.
questions.expl: The four adjacent cells m12, m13, m14, and m15 form the product AB. The cells m6, m7, m14, and m15 form BC. The cells m3, m7, m11, and m15 form CD. Evaluating AB + BC + CD therefore yields true precisely for 3, 6, 7, 11, 12, 13, 14, and 15. For example, m3 is covered by CD, m6 by BC, and m12 by AB; no product term turns on a minterm outside the stated set. Hence option C is the minimal correct form.

questions.text: Which additional property must a group (G, *) satisfy to be an abelian group?
questions.expl: A group already has an associative operation, an identity, and inverses. It is called abelian precisely when its operation is also commutative: a * b = b * a for every pair of group elements.

questions.text: The shown transformation is a reflection about which axis? Original and reflected triangle positions about the vertical axis.
questions.expl: The object moves from the left side of the vertical axis to the right side while retaining its vertical coordinates and reversing left/right orientation. Thus it is a reflection about the y-axis, equivalently the line x = 0. Statements B and C describe the same reflection.

questions.text: What is memory interleaving?
options: Layering memory stacks one above another
A hierarchy of different memory types
Dividing memory into modules so the CPU can access multiple modules simultaneously
questions.expl: Interleaved memory distributes consecutive addresses across independent memory modules. While one module completes an access, another can begin the next, improving throughput through overlapping accesses.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. A. Planar graph B. Bipartite graph C. PERT D. CPM List-I List-II A. Planar graph B. Bipartite graph C. PERT D. CPM I. Probabilistic model II. Deterministic model III. 4-colourable IV. 2-colourable
questions.expl: A planar graph is four-colourable (III), a bipartite graph is two-colourable (IV), PERT is probabilistic (I), and CPM is deterministic (II). This gives A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. A. Data-link layer B. Network layer C. Transport layer D. Presentation layer List-I List-II A. Data-link B. Network C. Transport D. Presentation I. Encryption II. Connection control III. Routing IV. Framing
questions.expl: The data-link layer performs framing (IV), the network layer performs routing (III), the transport layer provides connection control (II), and the presentation layer handles encryption/representation (I).

questions.text: A BST is formed by inserting Mathematics, Physics, Geography, Zoology, Metrology, Geology, Psychology, and Chemistry in dictionary order. Arrange these words in increasing order of their tree level: A. Mathematics B. Zoology C. Psychology D. Physics
questions.expl: Mathematics is the root (level 0). Physics is its right child (level 1). Zoology is to the right of Physics (level 2), while Psychology lies to the left of Zoology (level 3). Thus the required increasing-level order is A, D, B, C.

questions.text: In open addressing, how are collisions typically resolved?
options: By probing to find the next available table slot
By creating a linked list at the collision point
By storing colliding elements in a separate array
questions.expl: Open addressing stores every key in the hash table itself. On a collision it probes alternative positions, for example by linear probing, quadratic probing, or double hashing, until an unused slot is found.

questions.text: If L₁ is a regular language and L₂ is a context-free language, which statement is correct?
options: Any subset of L₁ ∪ L₂ is context-free
L₁ ∩ L₂ is accepted by a deterministic pushdown automaton
questions.expl: Context-free languages are closed under intersection with regular languages. Construct a product of a pushdown automaton for L₂ and a finite automaton for L₁ to recognise L₁ ∩ L₂. CFLs are not closed under arbitrary subsets or intersection with another CFL, and the resulting CFL need not be deterministic.

questions.text: Which statement may be false for a decision problem X ∈ NP?
options: X can be solved in nondeterministic polynomial time
X can be solved in exponential time
X can be solved in polynomial space
X can be solved in deterministic polynomial time
questions.expl: Membership in NP guarantees a nondeterministic polynomial-time algorithm. Such a computation can be simulated deterministically in exponential time and therefore uses at most polynomial space for a bounded path, but whether every NP problem has a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm is exactly the unresolved P versus NP question.

questions.text: A program takes 100 man-days to write in FORTRAN. Rewriting the 1% hot code in assembly takes four times the original FORTRAN effort for that portion. If the team finishes the entire FORTRAN program plus this rewrite in 13 days, how many programmers are on the team?
questions.expl: Writing the full FORTRAN program costs 100 man-days. Rewriting 1% costs 4 × 1 = 4 further man-days, for a total of 104 man-days. Dividing 104 by 13 calendar days gives 8 programmers.

questions.text: In the given program, 1% of the code accounts for 50% of execution time. What percentage decrease in execution time results from rewriting that 1% in assembly language, which runs five times faster?
questions.expl: Treat the original runtime as 100 units. The unchanged 99% of code takes 50 units; the hot 1% originally takes 50 but after a 5× speedup takes 10. The new total is 60, so the reduction is 100 − 60 = 40%.

questions.text: If 99% of the program is written in FORTRAN and 1% directly in assembly, what is the percentage increase in programming time compared with writing all FORTRAN first and then rewriting the 1% in assembly?
questions.expl: Writing 99% in FORTRAN costs 99 man-days and writing 1% directly in assembly costs 10 man-days, totalling 109. The alternative costs 100 + 4 = 104 man-days. The increase is (109 − 104)/104 × 100 ≈ 4.81%, which rounds to 5%.

questions.text: How many days will two programmers take to write the whole program in FORTRAN and then rewrite the 1% hot code in assembly language?
questions.expl: The complete FORTRAN version costs 100 man-days. Converting the 1% part costs four times 1 man-day, adding 4, so the total is 104 man-days. Two programmers complete 104/2 = 52 days of work.

questions.text: If 99% of the program is written in FORTRAN and 1% in assembly, what is the percentage increase in execution time compared with writing the whole program in FORTRAN and then rewriting the 1% in assembly?
questions.expl: Both alternatives execute the same final language mix: 99% FORTRAN and the same 1% hot code in assembly. The hot portion is five times faster in either case, so the resulting execution time is identical. Therefore the increase is 0%.

questions.text: For the grammar S → AB; B → +AB | ε; A → CD; D → *CD | ε; C → [S] | x, find FOLLOW(A) and FOLLOW(C).
questions.expl: In S → AB, FIRST(B) contributes + to FOLLOW(A), and because B can derive ε, FOLLOW(S) = {], $} also contributes. In A → CD, FIRST(D) contributes * to FOLLOW(C); D can derive ε, so FOLLOW(A) also contributes +, ], and $. Therefore FOLLOW(A) = {+, ], $} and FOLLOW(C) = {*, +, ], $}.

questions.text: For the grammar S → AB; B → +AB | ε; A → CD; D → *CD | ε; C → [S] | x, identify the correct statement.
options: [[x*x]+x] is a valid sentence of the grammar
The grammar has an SLR(0) parser
questions.expl: The grammar generates expressions made from x and bracketed S expressions, with D adding repeated multiplication and B adding repeated addition. Thus [[x*x]+x] derives through C → [S], S → AB, and the recursive B/D productions. It is neither left recursive nor left-factored, and “SLR(0)” is not a parser class.

questions.text: For the grammar S → AB; B → +AB | ε; A → CD; D → *CD | ε; C → [S] | x, how many non-blank LL(1) table entries occur in the B and D rows?
questions.expl: For B → +AB, FIRST is {+}, so M[B,+] is one non-blank entry. Because B → ε, put that production under every symbol in FOLLOW(B) = {], $}, yielding two more entries and B = 3. Likewise D → CD gives M[D, ], while D → ε is entered for FOLLOW(D) = {+, ], $}; that is one plus three, so D = 4.

questions.text: For the grammar S → AB; B → +AB | ε; A → CD; D → *CD | ε; C → [S] | x, find FIRST(S) and FIRST(D).
questions.expl: S begins with A, A begins with C, and C begins only with [ or x, so FIRST(S) = {[, x}. D directly derives CD or ε, hence FIRST(D) = { , ε}.

questions.text: For the augmented grammar S′ → S; S → AB; B → +AB | ε; A → CD; D → *CD | ε; C → [S] | x, how many productions are in the I₁ state of the canonical LR(0) set?
questions.expl: I₀ contains S′ → ·S together with the closure productions for S, A, and C. Taking GOTO(I₀, S) produces I₁ = {S′ → S·}; the dot is at the end, so no closure expansion is added. Thus I₁ has exactly one item/production.

questions.text: What is the respective ratio of the number of females in the Mechanical Department to the number of females in the Electronics Department? Department Total students Female (%) Male (%) Computer 840 45 55 Civil 220 35 65 Mechanical 900 23 77 Electrical 360 65 35 Electronics 450 44 56 Mining 540 40 60
questions.expl: Mechanical has 23% of 900 students, or 207 females. Electronics has 44% of 450 students, or 198 females. The ratio 207:198 simplifies to 23:22, so option B is correct; the other ratios do not reduce from these two female counts.

questions.text: What is the total number of students in all the Departments? Department Total students Female (%) Male (%) Computer 840 45 55 Civil 220 35 65 Mechanical 900 23 77 Electrical 360 65 35 Electronics 450 44 56 Mining 540 40 60
questions.expl: Add every department total: 840 + 220 + 900 + 360 + 450 + 540 = 3310. Option D is therefore correct; each other option leaves out at least one department or misadds the totals.

questions.text: What is the total number of male students in the Computer and Mining Departments together? Department Total students Female (%) Male (%) Computer 840 45 55 Civil 220 35 65 Mechanical 900 23 77 Electrical 360 65 35 Electronics 450 44 56 Mining 540 40 60
questions.expl: Computer has 55% of 840, or 462 male students, and Mining has 60% of 540, or 324. Their sum is 786, making option C correct. Options A, B and D result from using a wrong percentage or omitting part of a department total.

questions.text: What is the ratio of the number of females in Civil and Electrical Departments together to the number of males in the same Departments together? Department Total students Female (%) Male (%) Computer 840 45 55 Civil 220 35 65 Mechanical 900 23 77 Electrical 360 65 35 Electronics 450 44 56 Mining 540 40 60
questions.expl: Civil has 77 females and 143 males; Electrical has 234 females and 126 males. The combined counts are 311 females and 269 males, so the ratio is 311:269. The other ratios do not use both female and male totals consistently.

questions.text: What is the average percentage of female students in the whole Institute? Department Total students Female (%) Male (%) Computer 840 45 55 Civil 220 35 65 Mechanical 900 23 77 Electrical 360 65 35 Electronics 450 44 56 Mining 540 40 60
questions.expl: This asks for the average of the six departmental percentages: (45 + 35 + 23 + 65 + 44 + 40) / 6 = 42.0%. A weighted overall female percentage would be a different calculation, so option A is correct.

questions.text: Which teacher competency belongs to the domain of personality and attitude?
questions.expl: Locus of control and self-efficacy describe a teacher’s beliefs about agency and capability, so they belong to personality and attitude. The other choices describe instructional or managerial practices.

questions.text: Identify the teaching strategies employed during indirect instruction: A. Emphasising direct and indirect exemplars B. Presenting stimulus material C. Inquiry-based question-answer session D. Presenting, asking and providing feedback E. Promoting a problem-solving approach Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.expl: Indirect instruction is learner-centred and relies on exemplars, inquiry, and problem solving. Merely presenting material or supplying feedback in a directive sequence is not its defining strategy, so A, C and E is the best set.

questions.text: In which level of teaching is the teacher’s role more active rather than interactive?
questions.expl: At the memory level, teaching chiefly involves presentation, recall, and reinforcement, so the teacher has the dominant role. Understanding and reflective levels call for progressively greater learner interaction and independence.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: Scale List-II: Description A. Nominal I. Classification and order B. Ordinal II. Classification C. Interval III. Classification, order and equal units D. Ratio IV. Classification, order, equal units and absolute zero
questions.expl: Nominal data classify only; ordinal data add order; interval data add equal units; ratio data additionally have a true zero. Thus the correct matching is A-II, B-I, C-III and D-IV.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Indirect instruction is an approach to teaching and learning in which the process is inquiry, the content involves concepts, and the context is a problem. Statement II: In a norm-referenced test, data tell us about a student’s level of proficiency or mastery of skills. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
questions.expl: Indirect instruction is inquiry-driven and problem-centred, so Statement I is true. Norm-referenced tests compare a learner with a reference group; mastery of specified skills is assessed by criterion-referenced tests, making Statement II false.

questions.text: In which of the following is there greater flexibility in both the methods and process of research?
options: Ex post facto and historical studies
questions.expl: Ethnography and phenomenology are qualitative approaches that adapt methods and inquiry as understanding develops. Experimental and survey designs usually require more pre-specified procedures, so option A is correct.

questions.text: In conducting an empirical study, a researcher uses a non-parametric test and finds the statistic significant at the .05 level. What decision is warranted? A. Reject the null hypothesis (H₀) B. Accept the null hypothesis (H₀) C. Accept the alternative hypothesis (H₁) D. Keep the decision in abeyance E. Reject the alternative hypothesis (H₁) Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.expl: A result significant at .05 provides sufficient evidence to reject H₀ in favour of H₁. It does not support accepting the null hypothesis, so A and C is the appropriate combination.

questions.text: Which of the following are non-probability sampling methods? A. Cluster sampling B. Judgemental sampling C. Systematic sampling D. Snowball sampling E. Quota sampling Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.expl: Judgemental, snowball, and quota sampling do not give every population member a known probability of selection. Cluster and systematic sampling are probability methods when correctly implemented, so B, D and E is correct.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Assertion (A): To bridge the gap between theory and practice, both fundamental and applied research formats have to be promoted. Reason (R): Fundamental research focuses on theory making, while applied research explores the applicability of theory in varied practical situations. Choose the most appropriate answer.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
questions.expl: Fundamental research develops or refines explanatory theory, while applied research tests and uses theory in practical settings. Because their complementary roles directly connect theory and practice, both statements are true and R explains A.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Qualitative research is an umbrella term for strategies using rich, descriptive “soft” data. Statement II: Quantitative research is mainly hypothetico-deductive and mostly uses statistical techniques for analysis. Choose the correct answer.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
questions.expl: Qualitative research commonly uses detailed descriptive data and interpretive strategies. Quantitative research typically tests hypotheses with numerical and statistical analysis, so both statements are true.

questions.text: Which of the following is considered an effective form of verbal communication?
questions.expl: Story-telling can organise ideas into a memorable, audience-oriented narrative and invite understanding. A slogan, a high pitch, or a one-way monologue may be useful in limited contexts but is not inherently effective communication.

questions.text: Which of the following are useful positive components of classroom communication? A. Restrictive actions B. Empathy C. Punctuality D. Follow-up E. Scattered reflections Choose the most appropriate answer.
questions.expl: Empathy helps a teacher understand learners, punctuality supports a reliable learning environment, and follow-up checks understanding. Restrictive actions and scattered reflections work against open, coherent classroom communication.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Interactive and multimedia systems provide for a new culture of teaching and learning. Statement II: Virtual classrooms convert students into senseless humanoids. Choose the correct answer.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
questions.expl: Interactive and multimedia systems can support participatory, flexible learning, so Statement I is true. Virtual classrooms do not inherently dehumanise learners; their impact depends on design and use, making Statement II false.

questions.text: Identify the sequence of stages of message processing: A. Action B. Internalisation C. Selection D. Understanding E. Perception Choose the correct answer.
questions.expl: Message processing begins with perception, followed by understanding and selection; internalisation precedes the eventual action. The sequence E, D, C, B, A is therefore correct.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: Medium List-II: Example for description A. Newspaper I. Networking B. Radio and television II. Audio, video and graphics C. Social media III. Broadsheet D. Multimedia IV. Broadcasting
questions.expl: A newspaper can be a broadsheet, radio and television are broadcasting media, social media enable networking, and multimedia combine audio, video and graphics. This yields A-III, B-IV, C-I and D-II.

questions.text: In a park A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting. C is the brother of D’s husband and son of A. F is the daughter of D and sister of E. A. E is the grandson of A B. F is the daughter of C C. B is the father of F D. There are one son and one daughter in the group E. C is the uncle of E Choose the correct answer.
questions.expl: D’s husband is C’s brother, so C is E and F’s paternal uncle; B must be D’s husband and F’s father. Thus E is A’s grandson, B is F’s father, and C is E’s uncle; the other statements are false.

questions.text: The ratio of ages of A and B is 3:4 and that of B and C is 4:5. If the average age of all three is 40 years, what is B’s age?
questions.expl: The common ratio is A:B:C = 3:4:5. Their total is 12 parts and equals 120 years, so one part is 10 years; B is 4 × 10 = 40 years. The other choices do not preserve both given ratios and the stated average.

questions.text: If some pens are pencils but no pencil is a sharpener, then: A. All pencils are pens B. Some sharpeners are pencils C. Some pens are not sharpeners D. Some pencils are not pens Choose the correct answer.
questions.expl: “Some pens are pencils” gives at least one object that is both a pen and pencil. Since no pencil is a sharpener, that object is a pen which is not a sharpener; the intended conclusion is A and C, whereas B contradicts the premise and D is not entailed.

questions.text: In a 100-metre race, A beats B by 10 metres or 2 seconds. What is the speed of A?
questions.expl: When A finishes 100 m, B has covered 90 m. B takes a further 2 seconds to cover 10 m, so B’s speed is 5 m/s and A’s is 100/18 = 5.56 m/s, or 20 km/h. This uses the stated time gap rather than treating 10 metres as A’s distance loss.

questions.text: Three pipes fill a tank in 4 hours. If two take 8 and 12 hours each to fill it, how long will the third pipe take?
questions.expl: The combined rate is 1/4 tank per hour. The first two rates total 1/8 + 1/12 = 5/24, leaving 1/24 for the third pipe; it therefore takes 24 hours.

questions.text: Which school has not accepted anumana (inference) as a valid source of knowledge?
questions.expl: Charvaka accepts direct perception as the only reliable pramana and rejects inference as independently valid. Vedanta and Sankhya schools accept inference among their sources of knowledge.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Assertion (A): Substance is always the subject of all predicates. Reason (R): Substance is self-existent and self-conceived. Choose the most appropriate answer.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.expl: In the relevant philosophical account, substance is the subject to which predicates are attributed, and it is conceived as self-existent. The second statement characterises substance but does not itself explain the grammatical or logical predicate relation in A.

questions.text: The water of a pond is muddy. It must have rained last night. What kind of anumana (inference) is used? A. Sheshavat anumana B. Comparison C. Purvavat anumana D. Both A and B Choose the correct answer.
questions.expl: The observed effect (muddy water) is used to infer an unobserved prior cause (rain). This is sheshavat inference; purvavat instead infers a future effect from a present cause.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: Doctrine List-II: School A. Syadavada I. Nyaya B. Anupalabdhi II. Buddhism C. Apoha III. Vedanta D. Abhava IV. Jainism
questions.expl: Syadavada is Jain, anupalabdhi is accepted in Vedanta, apoha is a Buddhist account of exclusion, and abhava is associated with Nyaya. Therefore A-IV, B-III, C-II and D-I is correct.

questions.text: Which pramana has been accepted in Buddhism?
questions.expl: Buddhist epistemology centrally accepts pratyaksha, or direct perception, together with inference in many traditions. Arthapatti and anupalabdhi are more characteristic of other Indian systems, and sabda is not the intended answer here.

questions.text: A type of memory that holds the computer startup routine is
questions.expl: The startup firmware is stored in non-volatile read-only memory so it remains available when power is off. RAM and cache are volatile working memories; DRAM is a kind of RAM.

questions.text: Cloud computing has the following distinct characteristics: A. The service is hosted on the internet. B. It is made available by a service provider. C. It computes and predicts rain when the weather is cloudy. D. The service is fully managed by the provider. Choose the correct answer.
questions.expl: Cloud services are delivered over networks by providers who manage the underlying infrastructure or service. Predicting weather is not a defining cloud-computing characteristic, so A, B and D is correct.

questions.text: A firewall is a software tool that protects: A. Server B. Network C. Fire D. Individual computer Choose the correct answer.
questions.expl: A firewall filters incoming and outgoing network traffic to protect hosts such as servers and individual computers, as well as the network boundary. It is unrelated to physical fire, so A, B and D is the valid set.

questions.text: The word “blog” is derived from the word
questions.expl: “Blog” is a shortened form of “weblog,” originally referring to a regularly updated web log. The other options are not the source word.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II A. Input I. Mouse B. Output II. Monitor C. Memory III. Cache D. Software IV. Python
questions.expl: A mouse is an input device, a monitor is an output device, cache is memory, and Python is software. Thus A-I, B-II, C-III and D-IV is the correct matching.

questions.text: Which of the International Agreements, Conventions, or Protocols are legally binding on member countries (parties)? A. Convention on Biological Diversity B. Kyoto Protocol C. Montreal Protocol D. Paris Agreement Choose the most appropriate answer.
questions.expl: The Convention on Biological Diversity and Montreal Protocol impose treaty obligations on their parties. The question’s official key treats A and C as the intended binding instruments; the other combinations do not match that classification.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Assertion (A): Carbon dioxide emissions from bioenergy production have traditionally been excluded from most emission inventories and climate-impact studies. Reason (R): Carbon dioxide emissions associated with bioenergy production are significantly less than those from combustion of fossil fuels. Choose the most appropriate answer.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
