questions.expl: Bioenergy is often treated as carbon-neutral in inventories, which has led to emissions from its production being undercounted or excluded. Lower emissions relative to fossil fuels does not logically explain that accounting exclusion, so both statements are treated as true but R is not the explanation.

questions.text: Wind energy is very sensitive to wind velocity because wind power is directly proportional to the
questions.expl: The kinetic-energy flux in moving air varies with v³, so a small increase in wind speed produces a much larger increase in available wind power. Linear or square relationships underestimate this sensitivity.

questions.text: During physical treatment of wastewater, what is the correct order of operations? A. Flocculation B. Filtration C. Screening D. Sedimentation Choose the correct answer.
questions.expl: Screening first removes large debris, sedimentation allows settleable solids to drop out, flocculation aggregates fine particles, and filtration removes the remaining suspended matter. Hence C, D, A, B is the correct process order.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Assertion (A): Carbon monoxide is a serious asphyxiant; even a short exposure may have fatal health effects. Reason (R): Haemoglobin in blood has greater affinity for carbon monoxide than for oxygen. Choose the most appropriate answer.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
questions.expl: Carbon monoxide binds haemoglobin far more strongly than oxygen does, forming carboxyhaemoglobin and preventing oxygen transport. That mechanism directly explains why short, high exposures can cause severe hypoxia and death.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: Vedanga List-II: Subject A. Nirukta I. Phonetics B. Chhandas II. Ritual C. Shiksha III. Metrics D. Kalpa IV. Etymology
questions.expl: Nirukta concerns etymology, Chhandas metrics, Shiksha phonetics, and Kalpa ritual procedure. Therefore A-IV, B-III, C-I and D-II is the correct matching.

questions.text: Which of the following explain the concept of values? A. Values are beliefs tied inextricably to human emotion and behaviour. B. Values refer to desirable goals people strive to attain. C. Values are conflict-free. D. Values are ordered by importance relative to one another. E. Values are utilized primarily to effect change in a person’s knowledge. Choose the correct answer.
questions.expl: Values are enduring beliefs linked to emotion and behaviour, express desirable goals, and are arranged in a personal hierarchy of importance. They may conflict, and they are not confined to changing knowledge, so A, B and D is correct.

questions.text: Which of the following come under the mandate of the University Grants Commission (UGC)? A. Promotion and coordination of university education B. Determining and monitoring standards of teaching, examination and research in universities C. Organising continuous professional-development programmes for college and university teachers D. Framing regulations on minimum standards of education E. Disbursing and regulating grants to universities and colleges Choose the correct answer.
options: A, B, C and D only
B, C, D and E only
A, C, D and E only
A, B, D and E only
questions.expl: The UGC promotes and coordinates university education, sets and monitors standards, frames regulations, and allocates grants. Professional-development programmes may be supported by various bodies, but are not stated as the core statutory mandate in this item; hence A, B, D and E.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Equality of educational opportunities is a pre-condition for achieving equity in education. Statement II: Equity in education can be achieved without equality of educational opportunities. Choose the correct answer.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
questions.expl: Equal access to educational opportunities is a necessary foundation for equitable educational outcomes. Statement II denies that foundation, so Statement I is true and Statement II is false.

questions.text: What are the advantages of the Choice Based Credit System (CBCS) introduced by the UGC for higher education institutions? A. Focuses on student-centric education B. Allows students to choose interdisciplinary and intra-disciplinary courses C. Makes education at par with global standards D. Makes it easy to estimate student performance in terms of marks E. Offers flexibility for students to undertake studies at different times and institutions Choose the correct answer.
options: A, B, C and D only
B, C, D and E only
A, B, C and E only
C, D, E and A only
questions.expl: CBCS is student-centred, permits course choice across disciplines, supports comparability with broader credit systems, and offers mobility and flexibility. It is not principally designed merely to estimate performance in terms of marks, so A, B, C and E is correct.

questions.text: In an MBO organisation, management is through the identification of Through their work and the efforts of others, managers in industrial, educational, governmental and military organisations attempt to run their organisations with management by objectives (MBO) as an underlying concept. In MBO, senior and junior managers jointly identify common goals and define each individual’s responsibilities in terms of expected results. These measures guide unit operations and assess each member’s contribution. The process can include hourly employees. It integrates external managerial control with employee self-control and can apply at any level or in any size organisation. Effective functioning requir
questions.expl: The passage defines MBO as senior and junior managers jointly identifying the organisation’s common goals. The managers are participants in the process, not the thing through which management is identified.

questions.text: The requisite for management by objectives is centred on Through their work and the efforts of others, managers in industrial, educational, governmental and military organisations attempt to run their organisations with management by objectives (MBO) as an underlying concept. In MBO, senior and junior managers jointly identify common goals and define each individual’s responsibilities in terms of expected results. These measures guide unit operations and assess each member’s contribution. The process can include hourly employees. It integrates external managerial control with employee self-control and can apply at any level or in any size organisation. Effective functioning requires agreemen
questions.expl: MBO depends on managers and employees jointly setting goals and reviewing performance. That joint goal-setting makes participation—not one-sided senior control or a particular setting—the key requirement.

questions.text: The critical feature of this type of management is related to Through their work and the efforts of others, managers in industrial, educational, governmental and military organisations attempt to run their organisations with management by objectives (MBO) as an underlying concept. In MBO, senior and junior managers jointly identify common goals and define each individual’s responsibilities in terms of expected results. These measures guide unit operations and assess each member’s contribution. The process can include hourly employees. It integrates external managerial control with employee self-control and can apply at any level or in any size organisation. Effective functioning requires agr
options: Distinguishing operational roles between managers and workers
Sharing responsibility with an eye on results
questions.expl: MBO defines responsibility in terms of expected results and has managers and employees jointly agree on goals. Its central feature is therefore shared responsibility focused on outcomes, not rigid separation of roles.

questions.text: In this frame of reference, how does an organisation function effectively? Through their work and the efforts of others, managers in industrial, educational, governmental and military organisations attempt to run their organisations with management by objectives (MBO) as an underlying concept. In MBO, senior and junior managers jointly identify common goals and define each individual’s responsibilities in terms of expected results. These measures guide unit operations and assess each member’s contribution. The process can include hourly employees. It integrates external managerial control with employee self-control and can apply at any level or in any size organisation. Effective functioning
options: By including hourly employees in managerial positions
By identifying and executing performance targets in a collaborative mode
By imposing a rigid philosophy of management
By providing separate work environments for managers and workers
questions.expl: The passage says goals are jointly established in advance and performance is jointly reviewed. Collaborative identification and execution of targets, rather than rigid control or separate work environments, describes effective MBO functioning.

questions.text: The philosophy behind management by objectives is to Through their work and the efforts of others, managers in industrial, educational, governmental and military organisations attempt to run their organisations with management by objectives (MBO) as an underlying concept. In MBO, senior and junior managers jointly identify common goals and define each individual’s responsibilities in terms of expected results. These measures guide unit operations and assess each member’s contribution. The process can include hourly employees. It integrates external managerial control with employee self-control and can apply at any level or in any size organisation. Effective functioning requires agreement be
options: Effect improvement through a joint review of achievement of performance goals within a given timeframe
Integrate external and internal controls by managers
Provide managers scope to review accepted output variables
Agree upon different performance goals for managers and employees
questions.expl: MBO sets mutually agreed performance goals for a stated period and ends with a joint review against those goals. That review is intended to improve performance; the other options omit the essential shared, goal-based review.

questions.text: The number of positive integers not exceeding 100 that are either odd or the square of an integer is ____.
questions.expl: There are 50 odd integers through 100. Of the squares 1² through 10², the five even squares (2², 4², 6², 8² and 10²) are not already in the odd set, so the union has 50 + 5 = 55 integers. Counting all ten squares again would double-count the five odd squares.

questions.text: How many ways are there to pack six copies of the same book into four identical boxes, where a box can contain as many as six books?
questions.expl: Because both books and boxes are identical, each arrangement is a partition of 6 into at most four positive parts. The nine partitions are 6; 5+1; 4+2; 4+1+1; 3+3; 3+2+1; 3+1+1+1; 2+2+2; and 2+2+1+1.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs of propositions are not logically equivalent?
questions.expl: The first expression in option D requires r only when both p and q are true. The second requires r whenever either p or q is true, so they differ when exactly one of p and q is true. The other pairs are standard equivalent rewritings.

questions.text: Consider the linear programming problem: Maximise Z = 2x₁ + 3x₂ Subject to 2x₁ + x₂ ≤ 4; x₁ + 2x₂ ≤ 5; x₁, x₂ ≥ 0. The optimum value of the LP is
questions.expl: A linear-programming optimum occurs at a feasible corner. The two binding constraints give x₁ = 1 and x₂ = 2, so Z = 2(1) + 3(2) = 8. The other corners give smaller values.

questions.text: Consider a machine with byte-addressable main memory of 2¹⁶ bytes and block size 8 bytes. A direct-mapped cache has 32 lines. How many bits are in the tag, line, and word fields of a main-memory address?
questions.expl: A 2¹⁶-byte memory uses 16 address bits. An 8-byte block needs 3 word-offset bits and 32 cache lines need 5 line bits; the remaining 16 − 3 − 5 = 8 bits form the tag.

questions.text: The following basic-computer program is stored in memory. What is the accumulator content after execution? 210 CLA 211 ADD 217 212 INC 213 STA 217 214 LDA 218 215 CMA 216 AND 217 217 1234H 218 9CE2H
questions.expl: CLA clears AC; ADD 217 and INC produce 1235H, which STA stores at 217. LDA 218 loads 9CE2H, CMA gives 631DH, and 631DH AND 1235H equals 0215H.

questions.text: A non-pipeline system takes 50 ns per task. The same task uses a six-segment pipeline with a 10 ns clock. Determine the approximate speedup for 500 tasks.
questions.expl: Non-pipelined time is 500 × 50 = 25,000 ns. Pipeline time is (6 + 500 − 1) × 10 = 5,050 ns, including fill time. The speedup is 25,000/5,050 ≈ 4.95. A speedup of 6 ignores pipeline fill and drain overhead.

questions.text: What is the radix of the numbers if the solution to x² − 10x + 26 = 0 is x = 4 and x = 7?
questions.expl: By Vieta’s rule, the sum of the roots is the value represented by 10 in that radix. Since 4 + 7 = 11 in decimal, 10 in the unknown base is 11, so the base is 11.

questions.text: Consider the pseudocode with integers a and b, where a > 1 and a < b: int x = 0; int p = 1; while (p < b) { p = p * a; x = x + 1; } When the loop terminates, what is x in terms of a and b?
questions.expl: After x iterations, p = aˣ. The loop stops at the smallest integer x for which aˣ ≥ b, which is exactly ⌈logₐ b⌉. The floor is wrong whenever logₐ b is not an integer because it can leave p below b.

questions.text: In HTML, the <map> tag is used for
options: defining a path between two nodes in an image
defining clickable regions in an image
highlighting an area in an image
defining the site map of a website
questions.expl: The <map> element defines an image map, and its <area> elements specify clickable regions. It is unrelated to a navigation sitemap or visual highlighting.

questions.text: A compiler uses 1-byte chars, 2-byte shorts, 4-byte ints, and 8-byte doubles. Every primitive must begin at an address that is a multiple of its size; fields cannot be reordered. How much space is consumed by an array A[10] of this structure? struct { short s; char c; short t; char d; double r; int i; }
questions.expl: The layout is s at bytes 0–1, c at 2, padding at 3, t at 4–5, d at 6, then one byte of padding before double r at 8–15 and int i at 16–19. The structure is rounded to 24 bytes for 8-byte alignment, so ten elements occupy 240 bytes.

questions.text: Consider the recursive Java function: public static float f(long m, long n) { float result = (float)m / (float)n; if (m < 0 || n < 0) return 0.0f; else result -= f(m + 2, n * 3); return result; } Which real value best approximates f(1, 3)?
questions.expl: The recurrence alternates terms: 1/3 − 3/9 + 5/27 − 7/81 + …, stopping once m becomes negative in the recursive call chain. The partial sums settle near 0.2, whereas the larger choices ignore the alternating subtraction.

questions.text: The data node and name node in Hadoop are
options: Worker node and master node respectively
Master node and worker node respectively
questions.expl: DataNodes store and serve HDFS data blocks on worker machines. The NameNode maintains filesystem metadata and coordinates the cluster, so it is the master service.

questions.text: For S = (U, V, W, X, Y, Z), the functional dependencies are {U → V, VW → X, Y → W, X → U}. Which listed sets are candidate keys?
questions.expl: Z never appears on the right-hand side, so every key must contain Z. UYZ gives V from U and W from Y, then X from VW; VYZ gives W from Y, then X and U; XYZ gives U from X and then V. Each is minimal, yielding option D.

questions.text: A machine has 3 page frames and the reference stream A, B, C, D, A, B, E, A, B, C, D, E, B, A, B. If P and Q are the page faults under FIFO and LRU respectively, what is (P, Q)?
questions.expl: Simulating FIFO replaces the oldest loaded page and produces 11 faults. Simulating LRU instead evicts the least recently used page, which produces 12 faults for this sequence; replacement policies need not rank the same on every reference string.

questions.text: A disk has 60 cylinders. Requests are 10, 22, 20, 2, 40, 6, 38; the head starts at 20. Movement by one cylinder takes 2 ms. Under SSTF, what is the total service time?
questions.expl: SSTF serves 20, 22, 10, 6, 2, 38, 40, always choosing the nearest pending cylinder. The movement is 0 + 2 + 12 + 4 + 4 + 36 + 2 = 60 cylinders, and at 2 ms per cylinder the total is 120 ms; other totals result from a different service order.

questions.text: A Linux filesystem has 2 KB blocks and 32-bit disk addresses. An i-node has 12 direct pointers, one single-indirect pointer, and one double-indirect pointer. Approximately what is the largest representable file?
questions.expl: A 2 KB indirect block contains 2,048/4 = 512 addresses. The i-node addresses 12 + 512 + 512² blocks, about 262,668 blocks, which at 2 KB each is approximately 513 MB.

questions.text: In a single-level page-table system with the page table in memory, TLB hit rate is 80%. TLB search takes 15 ns and a main-memory access takes 150 ns. What is the effective memory access time?
questions.expl: On a TLB hit, time is 15 + 150 = 165 ns. On a miss, it is 15 + 2(150) = 315 ns because both the page table and the data are accessed. The weighted average is 0.8(165) + 0.2(315) = 195 ns; treating every reference as a hit would wrongly give 165 ns.

questions.text: Which UML diagram has a static view?
questions.expl: Use-case diagrams describe the actors and required system functionality without modelling a time-ordered execution. Collaboration, state-chart, and activity diagrams are behavioural or interaction views.

questions.text: Modifying software by restructuring is called
questions.expl: Perfective maintenance improves internal design, maintainability, efficiency, or other quality attributes after delivery; restructuring is a typical perfective change. Corrective maintenance fixes faults, while adaptive maintenance responds to a changed environment.

questions.text: A company can use languages L₁ and L₂; an application needs three times as many LOC in L₂ as in L₁. The project has 10 years of maintenance. For what LOC in L₁ are the total development-plus-maintenance costs equal? Parameter L₁ L₂ Man-years for development LOC/1000 LOC/1000 Development cost Rs. 70,000 Rs. 90,000 Maintenance cost per year Rs. 1,00,000 Rs. 40,000
questions.expl: For x lines of L₁, development costs are 70x and 270x rupees for L₁ and L₂ respectively, since the rates are per 1,000 LOC and L₂ needs 3x lines. Ten-year maintenance costs are Rs. 10,00,000 and Rs. 4,00,000; equating totals gives 70x + 10,00,000 = 270x + 4,00,000, hence x = 3,000 LOC.

questions.text: A software project is estimated at 864 function points. A six-person team has one requirements gatherer (Rs. 50,000/month), one designer (Rs. 70,000/month), two programmers (Rs. 60,000/month each), and two testers (Rs. 60,000/month each). Team productivity is 12 FP per person-month. What is the projected cost?
questions.expl: The effort is 864/12 = 72 person-months, or 72/6 = 12 calendar months for six people. Monthly payroll is 50,000 + 70,000 + 2(60,000) + 2(60,000) = Rs. 3,60,000, so the project cost is 12 × 3,60,000 = Rs. 43,20,000; it is not based on treating 864 as calendar months.

questions.text: A complete n-ary tree has either n children or no children at each node. If it has I = 10 internal nodes and L = 41 leaves, what is n?
questions.expl: For a full n-ary tree, L = (n − 1)I + 1 because each internal node contributes n outgoing edges. Substitution gives 41 = 10(n − 1) + 1, so 40 = 10(n − 1) and n = 5; the other arities do not yield 41 leaves.

questions.text: In a binary max heap containing n numbers, the smallest element can be found in what time?
questions.expl: A max heap only guarantees that the largest element is at the root. The smallest can be anywhere among the leaves, which are Θ(n) in number, so finding it requires a linear scan in the worst case.

questions.text: Algorithm A takes log₂(n) microseconds and algorithm B takes √n microseconds. What are the largest problem sizes they can solve in one second?
questions.expl: One second is 10⁶ microseconds. For algorithm A, log₂ n = 10⁶ gives n = 2¹⁰⁰⁰⁰⁰⁰; for algorithm B, √n = 10⁶ gives n = 10¹². Therefore option B is correct; 2²⁰ incorrectly treats the available time as only 20 microseconds.

questions.text: Let G be a directed graph on vertices 1 through 100. There is an edge i → j exactly when j = i + 1 or j = 3i. What is the minimum number of edges in a path from 1 to 100?
questions.expl: Breadth-first search gives the seven-edge path 1 → 3 → 9 → 10 → 11 → 33 → 99 → 100. The multiplication edges make it far shorter than increment-only travel, which would require 99 edges.

questions.text: Consider L = L₁ ∩ L₂, where L₁ = {0ᵐ1ᵐ20ⁿ1ⁿ | m, n ≥ 0} and L₂ = {0ᵐ1ⁿ2ᵏ | m, n, k ≥ 0}. Then L is
questions.expl: For a string to be in both languages, the portion after 2 in L₁ must be empty and the number of 1s before 2 must equal the number of 0s. Thus L reduces to {0ᵐ1ᵐ2 | m ≥ 0}, which is context-free but not regular.

questions.text: Let L₁ and L₂ over Σ = {a, b} be represented by (a* + b)* and (a + b)* respectively. Which statement is true?
questions.expl: The inner expression a* + b can generate either any run of a characters or a single b. Repeating it with the outer star generates every string over {a, b}, exactly as (a + b)* does. Therefore L₁ = L₂; neither language excludes a mixed a/b string.

questions.text: Which statement is true?
options: The union of two context-free languages is context-free.
The intersection of two context-free languages is context-free.
The complement of a context-free language is context-free.
Every context-free language can be accepted by a deterministic pushdown automaton.
questions.expl: Context-free languages are closed under union. They are not closed under intersection or complement, and deterministic PDAs recognise only the smaller class of deterministic context-free languages.

questions.text: Which of the following is not an intermediate code form?
questions.expl: Three-address code, quadruples, and postfix notation are linear intermediate-code representations used in translation. A syntax tree is a structural representation of the parsed program rather than an intermediate code sequence.

questions.text: A code has valid words 0000000000, 0000011111, 1111100000, and 1111111111. If the received word is 0000000111, which word was sent?
questions.expl: Decode by minimum Hamming distance. The received word differs from 0000011111 in two positions but from 0000000000 in three positions; the two words beginning with 11111 are farther away.

questions.text: Using RSA with p = 3, q = 11, and d = 7, find e and encrypt 19.
questions.expl: Here φ(n) = (3 − 1)(11 − 1) = 20. Since 7e ≡ 1 (mod 20), e = 3; with n = 33, encryption gives 19³ mod 33 = 28. Therefore option C is the only pair that has both the required inverse and ciphertext.

questions.text: Protocols in which the sender sends one frame and waits for an acknowledgement before sending the next frame are called
questions.expl: Stop-and-wait allows only one outstanding frame, so the sender must wait for its acknowledgement. Sliding-window protocols, unlike stop-and-wait, permit multiple frames in transit.

questions.text: The period of a signal is 100 ms. What is its frequency in kilohertz?
questions.expl: The signal period is 100 ms, and frequency is its reciprocal. Because 100 ms = 0.1 seconds, its frequency is 1/0.1 = 10 Hz. Dividing by 1,000 converts this to 0.01 kHz = 10⁻² kHz; therefore the correct option is D.

questions.text: The process of removing details from a given state representation is called
questions.expl: Abstraction deliberately suppresses irrelevant detail and retains features needed for reasoning. It is used to make a state space or problem representation manageable.

questions.text: Which statement is NOT true of problem solving in artificial intelligence?
options: It works on or implements a repetition mechanism.
questions.expl: AI problem-solving systems commonly use heuristic search and may handle incomplete or imprecise knowledge. A repetition mechanism is not a defining property of problem solving; it would often signal an undesirable loop.

questions.text: If f(x) means “x is my friend” and p(x) means “x is perfect”, translate: “Some of my friends are not perfect.”
questions.expl: “Some” requires an existential quantifier, and “not perfect” is ¬p(x). The witness must also be a friend, giving ∃x(f(x) ∧ ¬p(x)); a universal quantifier would incorrectly claim this for every friend.

questions.text: What kind of clauses occur in conjunctive normal form?
questions.expl: CNF is a conjunction of clauses, and each clause is a disjunction of literals. A literal may be a variable or its negation, so “variables” alone is too restrictive.

questions.text: On A = {a,b,c,d,e,f,g}, R = {(a,a),(b,b),(c,d),(c,g),(d,g),(e,e),(f,f),(g,g)}. Which listed property is satisfied: reflexive, antisymmetric, symmetric?
questions.expl: R is not reflexive because (c,c) and (d,d) are absent. It is antisymmetric because no distinct pair occurs in both directions, but it is not symmetric because (c,d) occurs without (d,c).

questions.text: For the premise ∀x(P(x) ∨ Q(x)), an argument tries to conclude (∀xP(x)) ∧ (∀xQ(x)) by instantiating P(c) ∨ Q(c) and then simplifying to P(c) and Q(c). Which assessment is correct?
options: Steps deriving P(c) and Q(c) are not correct inferences.
The universal-generalisation steps are not correct.
The final conjunction is not correct.
questions.expl: From a disjunction P(c) ∨ Q(c), one cannot infer either disjunct by simplification. Therefore the derivations of P(c) and Q(c) are invalid, and the later universal conclusions have no support.

questions.text: Which of the following are applications of a compiler symbol table? A. Storage allocation B. Checking type compatibility C. Suppressing duplicate-error messages
questions.expl: A symbol table records identifiers and their attributes. Compilers consult it for storage allocation and type checking, and it also lets them recognise a repeated declaration so duplicate diagnostics are controlled. Thus all three listed uses apply.

questions.text: Which simplified expressions represent F(A,B,C,D) = Σ(0,1,2,3,6,12,13,14,15)? A. A′B′ + AB + A′C′D′ B. A′B′ + AB + A′CD′ C. A′B′ + AB + BC′D′ D. A′B′ + AB + BCD′
questions.expl: A′B′ covers minterms 0–3 and AB covers 12–15. Expression B adds only minterm 6 through A′CD′, while D adds that same missing minterm through BCD′; the overlap at 14 is already covered by AB. In contrast, A and C also generate minterm 4, which is absent from the specified sum.

questions.text: For a k-segment pipeline, which statements are true? A. The theoretical maximum speed-up is k. B. A finite k-segment pipeline cannot attain that maximum exactly. C. All pipeline segments always take the same computation time.
questions.expl: With balanced stages and a long stream, speed-up approaches k, but fill and drain overhead prevent a finite workload from reaching it exactly. Equal stage times are an ideal design goal, not a universal property.

questions.text: Which statements about a multiprocessor system are true? A. It is controlled by one operating system. B. It consists of multiple computers connected by communication lines. C. It is classified as an MIMD system.
questions.expl: A multiprocessor is a tightly coupled system managed by one OS and normally follows the MIMD model. Statement B instead describes a distributed system of separate computers.

questions.text: Which statements regarding XML are true? A. XML is a set of tags designed to tell browsers how to display a web page. B. XML defines syntax for representing data, while the data meaning depends on the application. C. <Letter>, <LETTER>, and <letter> are different XML tags.
questions.expl: XML describes and transports structured data; it is not a display-language such as HTML. XML names are case-sensitive, so B and C are true.

questions.text: In 3D computer graphics, which statements are correct? A. Under perspective projection, parallel lines generally do not remain parallel, except lines parallel to the view plane. B. The perspective step uses a division by the depth coordinate after homogeneous transformation. C. Perspective transformation is linear.
questions.expl: Perspective makes parallel lines converge unless they are parallel to the image plane, and the perspective divide introduces the depth dependence. Because of that division, the resulting mapping is not linear.

questions.text: For Gouraud and Phong shading, which statements are true? A. Gouraud shading requires more computation than Phong shading. B. Gouraud shading interpolates vertex colours across a polygon. C. Phong shading interpolates vertex normals across a polygon.
questions.expl: Gouraud shading interpolates precomputed colours. Phong shading interpolates normals and evaluates lighting per pixel, so it is normally more computationally expensive; B and C are true.

questions.text: Two operations from a schedule conflict when A. at least one operation is a write, B. both access the same data item, and C. they belong to different transactions.
questions.expl: Conflicting operations are operations of different transactions on the same item where at least one writes. Two reads do not conflict, and operations on different data items do not conflict.

questions.text: Software reliability may be described with respect to A. execution time, B. calendar time, and C. clock time.
questions.expl: Reliability growth and failure intensity can be modelled against CPU/execution time, elapsed calendar time, or operational clock time. The appropriate time base depends on the system and measurement model.

questions.text: To create an object-behavioural model, an analyst A. evaluates use cases, B. builds a state-transition diagram, C. reviews the model for accuracy and consistency, and D. identifies events that do not drive an interaction sequence.
questions.expl: Use cases reveal the events and object responses, then state transitions model behaviour and the result is reviewed. Events that do not drive an interaction sequence are not part of that normal modelling step.

questions.text: Which are behavioural (black-box) testing techniques? A. Equivalence partitioning B. Graph-based testing C. Boundary-value analysis D. Data-flow testing E. Loop testing
questions.expl: Equivalence classes, boundary values, and graph-based tests derive tests from externally visible requirements or behaviour. Data-flow and loop testing require knowledge of program structure and are white-box techniques.

questions.text: The running time of an algorithm is O(g(n)) if and only if
options: its worst-case running time is O(g(n)) and its best-case running time is Ω(g(n)).
its worst-case running time is Ω(g(n)) and its best-case running time is O(g(n)).
questions.expl: An algorithm is O(g(n)) when its worst-case running time has an asymptotic upper bound g(n). The stated best-case lower-bound condition is compatible with that definition; the other assertions confuse O, Ω, and little-ω notation.

questions.text: Which statements are incorrect? A. Every tree is 2-colourable. B. A bipartite graph has no even-length cycles. C. A graph is 2-colourable if it is bipartite. D. A graph of maximum degree d can be coloured with d + 1 colours. E. A graph with O(|V|) edges can be coloured with O(log |V|) colours.
questions.expl: Trees are bipartite, and bipartite is equivalent to 2-colourable. A bipartite graph forbids odd cycles, not even ones. Sparsity alone does not force an O(log |V|)-colouring (a star is easy, but sparse graphs can still need more than that claimed bound in general).

questions.text: Which statements about hash functions are true? A. A hash function maps an arbitrary-length message to a fixed-length code. B. It maps a fixed-length message to a variable-length code. C. Distinct messages can have the same hash value.
questions.expl: A fixed-size digest is produced from inputs of arbitrary size. Since the input space is much larger than the digest space, collisions—different inputs with the same digest—are possible.

questions.text: Let G₁ and G₂ be arbitrary context-free grammars and R an arbitrary regular language. Which problems are undecidable? A. Is L(G₁) = L(G₂)? B. Is L(G₁) ⊂ L(G₂)? C. Is L(G₁) = R?
questions.expl: Equivalence and proper inclusion for arbitrary context-free languages are undecidable. Equality with a regular language is also undecidable: choosing R = Σ* would decide the undecidable universality problem for context-free grammars.

questions.text: Consider the languages L₁ = {aᶻ | z is an integer}, L₂ = {a²ᶻ | z > 0}, and L₃ = {ww | w ∈ {a,b}*}. Which are regular?
questions.expl: The first two languages are unary languages described by simple length patterns and are regular. The copy language {ww} requires matching an arbitrary string with itself, which is not regular.

questions.text: Which grammars are ambiguous? A. S → SS | aSb | bSa | a B. S → aSbS | bSaS | ε C. S → aAB; A → bBb; B → A | ε
questions.expl: Ambiguity means that one terminal string can have two different parse trees. The recursive alternatives in each listed grammar allow the same terminal sequence to be decomposed in more than one way; this is precisely why all three grammars are classified as ambiguous. A grammar need not have visibly identical productions to be ambiguous.

questions.text: Which cloud concept is related to pooling and sharing resources? A. Virtual memory B. Service C. Virtualization
questions.expl: Virtualization abstracts physical resources so they can be pooled and allocated to multiple users or services. Virtual memory and “service” are not the resource-pooling mechanism intended here.

questions.text: For Post Office Protocol (POP), which statements are true? A. POP has delete and keep modes. B. In delete mode, mail is deleted from the mailbox after retrieval. C. In delete mode, mail is deleted before retrieval. D. In keep mode, mail is deleted before retrieval. E. In keep mode, mail remains in the mailbox after retrieval.
questions.expl: POP can either retain server copies or delete them after successful retrieval. Thus A, B, and E are true; deletion before a client retrieves a message would defeat the protocol.

questions.text: A firewall can filter packets using which fields? A. Source IP address B. Destination IP address C. TCP source port D. UDP source port E. TCP destination port
questions.expl: Packet filters can inspect network-layer source and destination addresses and transport-layer source and destination ports for TCP or UDP. Every listed field is therefore usable in a firewall rule.

questions.text: A radical person is electable if the person is conservative, and otherwise is not electable. Which listed logical formalisation correctly represents that condition?
questions.expl: The intended proposition says that, for a radical person, electability holds exactly when conservatism holds. The matching formalisation preserves both the conditional case and the “otherwise not” case.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are true? A. Asentence a entails another sentence f if 8 is true in few worlds where @ is true. B. Forward chaining and backward chaining are very natural reasoning algorithms for knowledge bases in Horn form. C. Sound inference algorithms derive all sentences that are entailed. D. Propositional logic does not scale to environments of unbounded size.

questions.text: How many ways are there to place 8 indistinguishable balls into four distinguishable bins?
questions.expl: Placing n indistinguishable items into k distinguishable categories is solved by the stars and bars method. The number of ways equals: C(n + k - 1, k - 1) = C(n + k - 1, n). With n = 8 balls and k = 4 bins: C(8 + 4 - 1, 4 - 1) = C(11, 3) C(11, 3) = (11 * 10 * 9) / (3 * 2 * 1) = 990 / 6 = 165.

questions.text: Which of the following is principal conjunctive normal form for [(p ∨ q) ∧ ¬p → ¬q]?
questions.expl: Simplifying the propositional formula step by step: Evaluate the antecedent [(p ∨ q) ∧ ¬p]: (p ∧ ¬p) ∨ (q ∧ ¬p) = F ∨ (¬p ∧ q) = ¬p ∧ q. Rewrite the implication [¬p ∧ q] -> ¬q using the equivalence A -> B ≡ ¬A ∨ B: ¬(¬p ∧ q) ∨ ¬q Applying De Morgan's law: (p ∨ ¬q) ∨ ¬q = p ∨ ¬q. This expression is a single maxterm containing both literals p and q, which is its Principal Conjunctive Normal Form (PCNF).

questions.expl: Computing Euler's totient function for n = 45: Prime factorization of 45 is: 45 = 3^2 * 5. The distinct prime factors dividing 45 are p = 3 and p = 5. Applying Euler's product formula: phi(45) = 45 * (1 - 1/3) * (1 - 1/5) phi(45) = 45 * (2/3) * (4/5) phi(45) = 45 * (8/15) = 3 * 8 = 24.

questions.text: How many different Boolean functions of degree n are there?
questions.expl: A Boolean function of degree n maps n binary input variables to a single binary output: f: {0, 1}^n -> {0, 1}. The domain contains 2^n possible input combinations. For each of these 2^n inputs, the function can choose between 2 output values (0 or 1). By the product rule, the total number of distinct Boolean functions is: 2^(2^n).

questions.text: A Web application and its support environment has not been fully fortified against attack. Web engineers estimate that the likelihood of repelling an attack is only 30 percent. The application does not contain sensitive or controversial information, so the threat probability is 25 percent. What is the integrity of the web application?
questions.expl: In software security engineering, software integrity measures the system's resilience against unauthorized attacks: Integrity = 1 - (threat * (1 - security)) Given parameters: Threat probability = 25% = 0.25 Security (repel probability) = 30% = 0.30 Computing integrity: Integrity = 1 - (0.25 * (1 - 0.30)) Integrity = 1 - (0.25 * 0.70) Integrity = 1 - 0.175 = 0.825.

questions.text: A legacy software system has 940 modules. The latest release required that 90 of these modules be changed. In addition, 40 new modules were added and 12 old modules were removed. Compute the software maturity index for the system.
questions.expl: The Software Maturity Index (SMI) computed using the standard IEEE metric formula evaluates to approximately 0.849. SMI = [M_T - (F_c + F_a + F_d)] / M_T where: M_T = total number of modules = 940 F_c = number of changed modules = 90 F_a = number of added modules = 40 F_d = number of deleted modules = 12 Total modified components = F_c + F_a + F_d = 90 + 40 + 12 = 142. SMI = (940 - 142) / 940 SMI = 798 / 940 = 0.8489

Subtraction A - B is computed as A + (-B), where -B is represented as the 2's complement of B (invert bits and add 1). 2's complement eliminates end-around carry and provides a unique representation for zero (+0), unlike 1's complement. Inside f, a = 1 affects only the local parameter. *b = 2 writes 2 into variable i. c = 3 subsequently overwrites variable i with 3. Therefore, main prints 3, making statement S1 true. In program P2: Global variables are a = 1 a

questions.expl: Both Boolean equations simplify algebraically to their respective right-hand sides. Simplifying equation (i): LHS = wx + w(x + y) + x(x + y) = wx + wx + wy + xx + xy = wx + wy + x + xy Applying absorption laws (x + xy = x and x + wx = x): = x + wy = RHS. Thus, equation (i) is true. Simplifying equation (ii): Inside term: w x' (y + x z') = w x' y + w x' x z'. Because x' x = 0, the second term vanishes: w x' y + 0 = w

questions.text: Arrange the educational objectives of the cognitive domain from lower-order to higher-order skills. A. Evaluation B. Synthesis C. Analysis D. Knowledge E. Comprehension
questions.expl: Bloom's original cognitive hierarchy moves from Knowledge to Comprehension, then Analysis, Synthesis, and Evaluation. Thus D, E, C, B, A is the increasing order.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a criticism of the behaviourist model of teaching?
options: It does not take into account important internal processes that take place in the mind.
It is not appropriate for higher-order learning.
It is not appropriate for lower-order learning.
Learning is sometimes beyond the association between stimulus and response.
questions.expl: Behaviourism is particularly suited to observable, lower-order learning through stimulus-response practice and reinforcement. Its usual criticisms concern mental processes and more complex learning, so the claim about lower-order learning is not a criticism.

questions.text: Whether the results of a study can be generalized beyond the specific research context refers to:
questions.expl: External validity concerns whether findings apply beyond the people, setting, and conditions studied. Reliability is consistency, whereas internal validity concerns causal inference within the study.

questions.text: Assertion (A): Validity can never apply to any single proposition by itself. Reason (R): Validity and invalidity are attributes of arguments.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.
questions.expl: A proposition can be true or false, but validity evaluates whether an argument's conclusion follows from its premises. Since validity is an attribute of an argument rather than a standalone proposition, the Reason directly explains the Assertion.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: Source of Knowledge List-II: Accepted by A. Yogaja Pratyaksa I. Vedantins B. Kevalajnana II. Carvaka C. Only Pratyaksa III. Jaina D. Aparoksanubhuti IV. Nyaya
questions.expl: Nyaya accepts Yogaja perception, Jaina thought includes Kevalajnana, Carvaka accepts perception alone, and Vedanta recognizes Aparoksanubhuti. These pair as A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II A. Keyboard I. Memory B. Monitor II. Processor C. CPU III. Output device D. ROM IV. Input device
questions.expl: A keyboard is an input device, a monitor is an output device, the CPU is the processor, and ROM is memory. Therefore the matching is A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I.

questions.text: The SWAYAM was launched in __________.
questions.expl: SWAYAM, India's national online learning platform, was launched in 2017 to provide access to courses from school level through postgraduate study.

questions.text: National Education Policy 2020 has entrusted __________ with the responsibility to set up the standards of content, technology and pedagogy for online/digital teaching-learning.
questions.expl: NEP 2020 proposes the National Educational Technology Forum as the platform that will facilitate technology use and set standards for digital teaching-learning content, technology, and pedagogy.

questions.text: Which education policy first recommended 6% of GDP as public expenditure on education in India?
questions.expl: The National Policy on Education of 1968 first set the target of public expenditure on education reaching 6% of national income. Later policies reiterated rather than originated the target.

questions.text: The Black-foot disease is caused by the contamination of __________ in drinking water.
questions.expl: Blackfoot disease is a severe peripheral vascular disease associated with chronic arsenic exposure through drinking water. Cadmium, mercury, and lead cause different toxic effects.

questions.text: In quantitative research strategy, the principal orientation to the role of theory in relation to research is:
questions.expl: Quantitative research commonly begins with theory, derives hypotheses, and tests them with data. That theory-to-observation direction is deductive; induction instead builds theory from observations.

questions.text: Arrange the following in ascending order of their year of appearance, beginning with the oldest. A. Radio B. Television C. Book D. Prototypical Newspaper E. Film
questions.expl: Books predate newspapers; early newspapers predate film; radio follows film; and television is latest. Hence the chronological sequence is C, D, E, A, B.

questions.text: Arrange the following in ascending order of their moisture content. A. Trash B. Rubbish C. Refuse D. Garbage
questions.expl: Trash is the driest discarded material, followed by rubbish and then refuse, whereas garbage has the highest moisture content because it includes putrescible food waste. The increasing order is A, B, C, D.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: Convention/Protocol List-II: Related with A. Montreal Protocol I. Global Warming B. Stockholm Convention II. Transboundary movements of hazardous waste C. Kyoto Protocol III. Ozone layer depletion D. Basel Convention IV. Persistent organic pollutants
questions.expl: The Montreal Protocol addresses ozone depletion, the Stockholm Convention persistent organic pollutants, the Kyoto Protocol global warming, and the Basel Convention transboundary hazardous waste. The matching is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: Assertion (A): Eutrophication leads to depletion of dissolved oxygen in a lake. Reason (R): Dissolved oxygen in water decreases with increase in temperature.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.
questions.expl: Eutrophication adds nutrients, causing algal blooms whose decay consumes dissolved oxygen. Warmer water does hold less oxygen, so the Reason is true, but it is not the causal explanation of eutrophication's oxygen depletion.

questions.text: Assertion (A): Higher Education Institutions in the country with appropriate credit transfer mechanisms are facilitating students to enroll themselves in pre-designed academic programmes. Reason (R): Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) works on the principle of multiple entry-multiple exit as well as anytime, anywhere and any-level learning.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.
questions.expl: The Academic Bank of Credits supports portable, accumulated credits and flexible pathways including multiple entry and exit. That flexibility does not imply that institutions are facilitating enrolment only in pre-designed programmes, so the Assertion is false while the Reason is true.

questions.text: Assertion (A): The influence of mass media is rarely direct. Reason (R): According to Limited Effects theories, media effects are almost always mediated by group membership or relationships.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.
questions.expl: Limited-effects approaches hold that interpersonal relations, groups, and social context mediate media influence. This mediation explains why mass-media effects are rarely simple or directly imposed on individuals.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a programming language?
questions.expl: Python, C, and Java are programming languages used to write software. Google is a company and search service, not a programming language.

questions.text: USB stands for:
questions.expl: USB is short for Universal Serial Bus, the standard interface used to connect peripherals and transfer data and power.

questions.text: Arrange the following phrases in the vision of the National Education Policy, 2020 in the correct sequence of their appearance. A. A conscious awareness of one's roles and responsibilities in a changing world B. An education system rooted in Indian Ethos C. Developing a deep sense of respect towards the fundamental duties and constitutional values D. Transforming Bharat into an equitable and vibrant knowledge society E. Instilling among learners a deep-rooted pride in being Indian
questions.expl: The policy vision begins with an education system rooted in Indian ethos and its aim of transforming Bharat into an equitable, vibrant knowledge society, then states constitutional duties, responsibility in a changing world, and pride in being Indian. This gives B, D, C, A, E.

questions.text: The incomes of A and B are in the ratio 3 : 2 and their expenses are in the ratio 5 : 3. If each of them saves Rs. 3,000, then A's income is:
questions.expl: Let incomes be 3x and 2x and expenses be 5y and 3y. Savings give 3x - 5y = 3000 and 2x - 3y = 3000. Solving gives y = 3000 and x = 6000, so A's income is 3x = Rs. 18,000.

questions.text: Complete the following series: 582, 581, 585, 576, 592, 567, ______
questions.expl: The successive changes alternate as -1, +4, -9, +16, -25: negative and positive squares. The next change is +36, so 567 + 36 = 603.

questions.text: A person who believes that all social, political, economic and cultural change is inevitably based on the development and diffusion of technology is a:
questions.expl: Technological determinism treats technological development and diffusion as the decisive driver of social and cultural change. The other labels give primacy to different forces or reject that determinist claim.

questions.text: In everyday conversation, when people make reference to paying attention, planning, forgetting, guessing, daydreaming and so on, they are invoking:
questions.expl: Paying attention, planning, forgetting, guessing, and daydreaming describe mental processes. They are cognitive concepts, unlike propaganda or forms of false information.

questions.text: Which of the following are TRUE? A. For the Nyaya, knowledge of Abhava is acquired through Anupalabdhi Pramana. B. The Nyaya makes a distinction between Laukika and Alaukika Pratyaksa. C. The Nyaya reduces Arthapatti to Anumana. D. The Nyaya accepts the validity of Upamana as a Pramana.
questions.expl: Nyaya recognizes ordinary and extraordinary perception, treats arthapatti as inferential rather than an independent means, and accepts comparison as upamana. It does not accept anupalabdhi as a separate pramana for absence, making B, C, and D true.

questions.text: Which of the following memories/storage are volatile? A. RAM B. ROM C. Cache D. SSD E. HDD
questions.expl: RAM and cache lose their stored contents when power is removed, so both are volatile. ROM, SSDs, and HDDs are non-volatile storage.

questions.text: Which of the following renewable energy resources contributes the highest proportion to the total installed power capacity in India?
questions.expl: Among renewable technologies, solar has the largest installed capacity in India. Nuclear power is not conventionally classified as renewable, while wind and hydro have lower installed capacity than solar.

questions.text: Identify the correct mathematical statements. A. A batsman makes a score of 87 runs in the 17th inning and thus increases his average by 3. Then his average after the 17th inning is 36. B. The value of a number subtracted from the numerator and denominator of the fraction 6/7 to obtain a fraction equal to 3/4 is 3. C. If 15% of 40 is greater than 25% of a number by 2, then the number is 16. D. (1 + 1/2)(1 + 1/3)(1 + 1/4)...(1 + 1/120) = 60.5
questions.expl: For A, the prior total is 16 x 33 = 528, so adding 87 gives 615/17, not 36. For B, (6-x)/(7-x)=3/4 gives x=3. For C, 6=0.25n+2 gives n=16. For D, the product telescopes to 3/2 x 4/3 x ... x 121/120 = 121/2 = 60.5; hence B, C, and D are true.

questions.text: Match the words with their codes. List-I: Word List-II: Code A. CRAB I. 32 B. BARK II. 49 C. OVER III. 24 D. SING IV. 60
questions.expl: The code is the sum of the positions of the letters: CRAB = 3+18+1+2 = 24, BARK = 2+1+18+11 = 32, OVER = 15+22+5+18 = 60, and SING = 19+9+14+7 = 49. Thus A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.text: "Sound is eternal, because it is caused" commits the fallacy (hetvabhasa) of:
questions.expl: A cause is ordinarily a mark of production and hence impermanence, not eternity. The stated reason therefore establishes the contrary of the conclusion, which is the viruddha fallacy.

questions.text: During which of the following years was the manufacturing of product A approximately equal to the average production of that year? The values represent the number (in thousands) of five types of products manufactured in different years. Year A B C D E 2021 29 45 26 15 32 2022 32 52 58 26 35 2023 28 54 92 24 39 2024 26 58 86 27 34 2025 23 63 82 28 34
questions.expl: For 2021, total production is 29+45+26+15+32 = 147, so the average is 147/5 = 29.4, approximately product A's 29. The other listed years have much larger gaps.

questions.text: Manufacturing of product C in 2023 was approximately what percent of the total production of product B in 2022 and 2024 together? The values represent the number (in thousands) of five types of products manufactured in different years. Year A B C D E 2021 29 45 26 15 32 2022 32 52 58 26 35 2023 28 54 92 24 39 2024 26 58 86 27 34 2025 23 63 82 28 34
questions.expl: Product C in 2023 is 92. Product B in 2022 and 2024 totals 52+58=110. Thus 92/110 x 100 = 83.64%, approximately 84%.

questions.text: If we consider the combined production of products C and E in each year, what is the difference between their combined production in 2023 and 2025? The values represent the number (in thousands) of five types of products manufactured in different years. Year A B C D E 2021 29 45 26 15 32 2022 32 52 58 26 35 2023 28 54 92 24 39 2024 26 58 86 27 34 2025 23 63 82 28 34
questions.expl: For 2023, C+E = 92+39 = 131 thousand. For 2025, C+E = 82+34 = 116 thousand. The difference is 15 thousand, or 15,000.

questions.text: During which of the following years did product B have the lowest percentage of manufacturing with reference to the combined manufacturing of that year? The values represent the number (in thousands) of five types of products manufactured in different years. Year A B C D E 2021 29 45 26 15 32 2022 32 52 58 26 35 2023 28 54 92 24 39 2024 26 58 86 27 34 2025 23 63 82 28 34
questions.expl: The B shares are 45/147, 52/203, 54/237, and 58/231 for 2021-24. The 2023 share, about 22.8%, is the lowest.

questions.text: Manufacturing of product D in 2021 is approximately less by what percent of its production in 2024? The values represent the number (in thousands) of five types of products manufactured in different years. Year A B C D E 2021 29 45 26 15 32 2022 32 52 58 26 35 2023 28 54 92 24 39 2024 26 58 86 27 34 2025 23 63 82 28 34
questions.expl: Product D rises from 15 in 2021 to 27 in 2024. The shortfall relative to 2024 is (27-15)/27 x 100 = 44.44%, approximately 44%.

questions.text: Choose the correct statements. A. Diagnosis of the learners is done in the Inter-Active stage of teaching. B. Feedback and testing of the learners are done in the Post-Active stage of teaching. C. Fixing up goals and content are done in the Post-Active stage of teaching. D. Selection of appropriate testing devices is done in the Post-Active stage of teaching. E. Decision about strategies of teaching is done in the Post-Active stage of teaching.
questions.expl: The interactive stage includes diagnosing learners. Post-active work includes evaluation, feedback, testing, and choosing assessment devices. Goals, content, and teaching strategies are pre-active planning tasks, so A, B, and D are correct.

questions.text: Match the lesson-planning concepts with their descriptions. List-I List-II A. Concept Mapping I. Graphical tools for organizing and representing knowledge B. Five E-based Lesson Planning II. Constructive Approach C. Stimulus-response-based lesson planning III. Systematic arrangement of subject matter D. Unit Plan IV. Behaviourist Approach
questions.expl: Concept mapping uses graphical knowledge representations; the Five E model is constructivist; stimulus-response planning is behaviourist; and a unit plan systematically arranges subject matter. Hence A-I, B-II, C-IV, D-III.

questions.text: Identify the advantages of open-ended questions in survey research. A. It is easy to process answers. B. Respondents can answer in their own terms. C. They enhance the comparability of answers. D. They are useful for exploring new areas or areas in which the researcher has limited knowledge.
questions.expl: Open-ended questions let respondents frame answers in their own words and are useful for exploratory work. Their answers are usually harder to code and less directly comparable than standardized closed responses, leaving B and D.

questions.text: Match the communication groups with their characteristics. List-I: Types of groups in communication List-II: Characteristic A. Primary Group I. Members interact with one another to benefit an audience B. Self-Help Group II. Goal is to improve members' skills C. Learning Group III. Membership is based on sentiment D. Public Group IV. All members have a common problem
questions.expl: Primary groups rest on sentiment, self-help groups share a common problem, learning groups improve members' skills, and public groups communicate for an audience. The matching is A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

questions.text: Which of the following are TRUE? A. For the Carvaka, Pratyaksa is the only pramana. B. For the Carvaka, Sabda is the only pramana. C. For the Carvaka, Anumana is not a pramana. D. For the Jaina, Mati includes both perceptual and inferential knowledge.
questions.expl: Carvaka treats direct perception as the only valid pramana and rejects inference and verbal testimony as independent knowledge sources. In Jaina epistemology, mati includes perceptual and inferential cognition, so A, C, and D are true.

questions.text: Match the sampling methods with their descriptions. List-I List-II A. Snowball I. Handpicked cases on the basis of specific suitability B. Purposive II. Equivalent of stratified sampling C. Quota III. Choosing the nearest individuals to serve as respondents D. Convenience IV. Identifying other respondents with the help of initial respondents
questions.expl: Snowball sampling obtains further respondents through initial respondents; purposive sampling selects cases for suitability; quota sampling parallels stratification; and convenience sampling chooses nearby available people. Thus A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

questions.text: Arrange the following intervals of the standard normal variate in increasing order of probabilities. A. 0 <= Z <= +1 B. +1 <= Z <= +2 C. +2 <= Z <= +3 D. +3 <= Z < +infinity
questions.expl: The standard normal density is greatest near zero and declines in the positive tail. Therefore the probability is smallest beyond +3, then from +2 to +3, then +1 to +2, and largest from 0 to +1: D, C, B, A.

questions.text: Arrange the following operating systems in the correct chronological order of their development. A. Linux B. MS-DOS C. MAC OS D. Windows
questions.expl: MS-DOS 1.0 appeared in 1981, the original Macintosh and its system software in 1984, Windows 1.0 in 1985, and Linux in 1991. The increasing chronology is B, C, D, A.

questions.text: Arrange the following fractions in descending order. I. 9/11 II. 8/9 III. 4/7 IV. 3/5 V. 8/15
questions.expl: The values are 8/9 about 0.889, 9/11 about 0.818, 3/5 = 0.6, 4/7 about 0.571, and 8/15 about 0.533. In descending order this is II > I > IV > III > V.

questions.text: Match the HECI bodies with their functions. Body under HECI Function A. NHERC I. Accreditation of higher education institutions B. NAAC II. Single-point regulator for higher education sector C. HEGC III. Formulating a National Higher Education Qualification Framework D. GEC IV. Funding and financing of higher education
questions.expl: Under HECI, NHERC is the single-point regulator, NAAC handles accreditation, HEGC handles funding and financing, and GEC develops the National Higher Education Qualification Framework. Therefore A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

questions.text: In simple terms, the first line of the passage means: The use of the term dharma for law, nevertheless, was neither universal nor inevitable. This is borne out by the first century C.E. author Kautilya's compendium Treatise on Politics (Arthasastra). The significance of Kautilya's work for the history of law in India rests primarily on the fact that it provides a different and in many respects unique lens into that history. His treatise belongs to a distinct scholarly tradition with social and political priorities different from those represented by the science of dharma (dharmasastra), the primary discipline devoted to jurisprudential reflection within the Brahmanical scholastic tradition.
options: There was nothing unavoidable or locally acceptable about the use of the word 'law' for 'dharma', anyway.
There was nothing inevitable or meaningful about the use of the word 'dharma' for law, anyway.
There was nothing unavoidable or globally acceptable about the use of the word 'dharma' for 'law', anyway.
There was nothing permanent or unavoidable about the use of the word 'dharma' for law, anyway.
questions.expl: The passage says that calling law dharma was neither universal nor inevitable. 'Globally acceptable' conveys universal and 'unavoidable' conveys inevitable, which makes option C the closest paraphrase.

questions.text: The work of Kautilya is of significance because: The use of the term dharma for law, nevertheless, was neither universal nor inevitable. This is borne out by the first century C.E. author Kautilya's compendium Treatise on Politics (Arthasastra). questions.expl: The Linux Virtual File System (VFS) uses four principal object types, and the superblock is the one that represents a whole mounted file system, holding metadata such as its type, size, and status. questions.text: Consider a B⁺ tree in which the maximum number of keys in a node is 5. What is the minimum number of keys in any non-root node?
questions.expl: In a B⁺ tree, the maximum number of keys per node equals the order n minus 1, so a maximum of 5 keys gives n - 1 = 5, meaning order n = 6. Minimum keys in a non-root node = ⌈n/2⌉ - 1 = ⌈6/2⌉ - 1 = 3 - 1 = 2 Every non-root node must therefore hold at least 2 keys to keep the tree at least half full.

questions.text: Based on the passage, including the 10% contingency margin, what is the project cost? A project is planned for an enterprise accounting system with an estimated size of 60 KLOC. The organization applies Basic COCOMO in Semi-Detached mode, using these parameters: Effort = 3.0 x (KLOC)^1.0 person-months Development time = 2.5 x (Effort)^0.5 months Average cost per person-month (PM) = $10,000 A contingency margin of 10% on effort is mandatory The client demands a detailed schedule if staff is capped at 15 engineers
questions.expl: Basic COCOMO first gives the nominal effort from project size, and then the mandatory contingency margin is layered on before costing the project. Nominal effort = 3.0 × (60)^1.0 = 180 PM Effort with 10% contingency = 180 × 1.10 = 198 PM Project cost = 198 PM × $10,000 per PM = $1,980,000 $1,980,000 is $1.98 M, the contingency-inclusive project cost.

questions.text: Based on the passage, what is the estimated development time in months? A project is planned for an enterprise accounting system with an estimated size of 60 KLOC. The organization applies Basic COCOMO in Semi-Detached mode, using these parameters: Effort = 3.0 x (KLOC)^1.0 person-months Development time = 2.5 x (Effort)^0.5 months Average cost per person-month (PM) = $10,000 A contingency margin of 10% on effort is mandatory The client demands a detailed schedule if staff is capped at 15 engineers
questions.expl: COCOMO's schedule equation is applied to the nominal effort estimate, the 180 PM figure computed before the contingency margin is added, since the contingency margin covers extra staffing risk rather than changing the underlying size-based schedule model. The organization applies Basic COCOMO in Semi-Detached mode, using these parameters: Effort = 3.0 x (KLOC)^1.0 person-months Development time = 2.5 x (Effort)^0.5 months Average cost per person-month (PM) = $10,000 A contingency margin of 10% on effort is mandatory The client demands a detailed schedule if staff is capped at 15 engineers
questions.expl: Average staffing level is the total effort divided by the calendar time it is spread across, using the same nominal-effort basis adopted for the development time calculation above. Average staffing = Effort / Development time Average staffing = 180 PM / 33.5 months ≈ 5.37 engineers Rounding to the nearest whole engineer gives approximately 5 engineers, the closest listed option.
