questions.text: What can be ascribed to learning styles? A. They describe how a student learns. B. They are learners’ strengths and preferences in responding to environmental stimuli. C. They describe what a learner learns. D. They are behavioural patterns developed for new learning.
questions.expl: Learning styles concern preferences and patterns in how a learner approaches learning, not the subject matter being learned. Therefore A, B, and D fit, while C does not.

questions.text: What can be correctly inferred about the traditional teaching method and support system? A. The teacher controls the class and teaches using a blackboard. B. It is also called the Back-to-Basics system. C. The student is responsible for using self-learning tools. D. Virtual labs are a teaching tool. E. Charts, maps, textbooks and teacher handouts are prime resources.
questions.expl: Traditional instruction is teacher-led and commonly relies on blackboards, textbooks, charts and handouts. Self-learning tools and virtual laboratories belong more naturally to learner-centred or technology-supported approaches.

questions.text: What is incorrect about SWAYAM Prabha?
options: It was launched by Sri Abul Kalam Azad.
Satellite is used to telecast educational content through DTH channels.
Its web portal is maintained by INFLIBNET, Gujarat.
Its content is provided by NPTEL, IITs, UGC, CEC and IGNOU.
questions.expl: SWAYAM Prabha is a DTH educational initiative supported by national educational institutions. The attribution to Sri Abul Kalam Azad is incorrect; the other statements describe its delivery and content ecosystem.

questions.text: A researcher tells participants something false about a research session in order to mislead them. The researcher is using:
questions.expl: Active deception deliberately supplies false information to participants. Ethical research requires that such deception be justified, minimized, and followed by appropriate debriefing.

questions.text: Which research criterion relates mainly to causality?
questions.expl: Internal validity asks whether the observed effect can credibly be attributed to the proposed cause rather than confounding factors. External validity concerns generalisation.

questions.text: Arrange these data sets in increasing order of coefficient of variation. A. x̄ = 8, σ = 1.7 B. x̄ = 11, σ = 2.2 C. x̄ = 15, σ = 3.6 D. x̄ = 16, σ = 3
questions.expl: Because coefficient of variation is σ/x̄ × 100, it compares dispersion relative to each data set’s mean. The values are D 18.75%, B 20%, A 21.25%, and C 24%; therefore the increasing order is D, B, A, C.

questions.text: According to UGC Regulations 2018 on plagiarism, which similarities constitute Level-1 plagiarism? A. 12% B. 42% C. 28% D. 56% E. 37%
questions.expl: UGC’s Level-1 plagiarism band is above 10% up to 40%. Thus 12%, 28%, and 37% qualify. Both 42% and 56% exceed that ceiling and therefore fall in higher plagiarism bands.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II A. Nominal I. Satisfaction level B. Ordinal II. Weight C. Interval III. Ethnicity D. Ratio IV. Year of death Variable types and examples.
questions.expl: Nominal data classify ethnicity, ordinal data rank satisfaction, interval data include years with equal intervals but no true zero, and weight is ratio-scale data with a true zero.

questions.text: Which is the first newspaper published in India in modern times?
questions.expl: Hickey’s Bengal Gazette, started by James Augustus Hicky in 1780, is generally recognised as the first printed newspaper in India.

questions.text: Which cannot be treated as a folk tradition of communication in India?
questions.expl: Jatra, Ramleela and Kumbh Mela are traditional cultural forms or gatherings that transmit shared meanings. Cinema is a modern mass-medium form rather than a folk communication tradition.

questions.text: Arrange the 5 Ws of communication in proper sequence. A. Why B. When C. What D. Who E. Where
questions.expl: A common planning sequence begins with who, then what, when, where and why. It identifies the communicator or audience before message, timing, place and purpose.

questions.text: Three major actions in the process of communication are: A. Receiving B. Sending C. Reviewing D. Interpreting E. Analysing
questions.expl: Communication entails sending a message, receiving it, and interpreting it. Reviewing and analysing can support communication but are not the basic three actions.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II A. Interviews I. Group communication B. Newspaper II. Intrapersonal communication C. Classroom III. Interpersonal communication D. Meditation IV. Mass communication Applications and communication terms.
questions.expl: Interviews are interpersonal communication, newspapers are mass communication, a classroom is group communication, and meditation is intrapersonal communication.

questions.text: A person sold an item at a loss of 7%. Had they sold it at a gain of 7.5%, they would have received ₹87 more. What is the cost price?
questions.expl: The difference between a 7.5% gain and a 7% loss is 14.5% of the original cost price. Therefore 0.145 × CP = 87 and CP = ₹600. The two selling-price scenarios are compared against the same cost price.

questions.text: In a 500 m race, A beats B by 20 m and C by 80 m. If B and C run 100 m at the same speeds, by how many metres will B beat C?
questions.expl: This race comparison uses the same speeds as before. Because A covers 500 m while B and C cover 480 m and 420 m, B:C speed ratio is 480:420 = 8:7. In the 100 m race B finishes while C covers 87.5 m, leaving 12.5 m.

questions.text: Arrange the fractions in increasing order. A. 12/17 B. 13/19 C. 8/11 D. 16/23
questions.expl: Compare the listed fractions by their decimal values: B ≈ .684, D ≈ .696, A ≈ .706 and C ≈ .727. Therefore the increasing order is B, D, A, C; no fraction is larger merely because its numerator is larger.

questions.text: Identify the numbers that occur in the series 1, 7, 17, 31, 49, … A. 74 B. 95 C. 97 D. 127 E. 161
questions.expl: To identify which numbers occur in the series, inspect the successive differences: 6, 10, 14 and 18 increase by 4 each time. Continuing gives 71, 97, 127 and 161; therefore C, D and E occur, while 74 and 95 do not.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II A. QUAKE I. KTFUL B. OFTEN II. VHQDU C. PEACH III. IEYOU D. DRIVE IV. JUYWR Words and unique codes.
questions.expl: The coded words follow the given unique-code correspondences: QUAKE–JUYWR, OFTEN–KTFUL, PEACH–VHQDU and DRIVE–IEYOU.

questions.text: Identify the pattern of argument in: “Habits are like a cable. We weave a strand of it every day and soon it cannot be broken.”
questions.expl: The statement explains habits by comparing them to a cable built strand by strand. Reasoning by a relevant comparison is an argument from analogy.

questions.text: What can be correctly inferred? “You know how I know animals have souls? Because, on average, the lowest animal is a lot nicer and kinder than most human beings that inhabit this Earth.” A. The kindness claim is a premise. B. Animals have souls is a premise. C. It is not an argument. D. The kindness claim is the conclusion. E. Animals have souls is the conclusion.
questions.expl: The kindness claim is offered as a reason, so it is the premise. “Animals have souls” is what the speaker seeks to establish, making it the conclusion.

questions.text: What can be inferred from: “No musicians are Greeks. All traders are musicians. Therefore, no traders are Greeks.” A. It is figure II. B. It is an EAE mood. C. Greeks is the major term. D. The minor term of the conclusion is distributed. E. The middle term is undistributed.
questions.expl: The premises and conclusion have E-A-E form. “Greeks” is the predicate of the conclusion (major term), and “traders,” the subject of the E conclusion, is distributed; the middle term musicians is distributed in the first premise.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II A. Anyonyabhava I. Hare’s horn B. Atyantabhava II. Non-existence of the jar now C. Pragabhava III. This is not that D. Pradhvamsabhava IV. Temporary absence of a thing Forms of non-existence and representations.
questions.expl: Anyonyabhava is mutual non-existence (“this is not that”); atyantabhava is absolute non-existence (hare’s horn); pragabhava is prior absence; pradhvamsabhava is absence after destruction.

questions.text: Among the following, which is correct in the context of Sabda Pramana?
options: For Samkhya, a word signifies a universal.
For Jainas, a word signifies a particular.
For old Nyaya, a word symbolizes a universal only.
For Vedantins, a word primarily means the class character of individuals.
questions.expl: In the Samkhya account, a word primarily conveys the universal. The other statements oversimplify or misstate the relevant schools’ accounts of word meaning.

questions.text: If (L)ₘ represents a number L in base-M, what is the value of (107)₁₆ + (257)₁₆?
questions.expl: Because hexadecimal uses base 16, convert each number before adding: (107)₁₆ = 1×256 + 0×16 + 7 = 263 and (257)₁₆ = 2×256 + 5×16 + 7 = 599. Therefore their decimal sum is 862, or (862)₁₀.

questions.text: In computer networking, an IPv6 address is how many times larger than an IPv4 address?
questions.expl: IPv4 uses 32 bits and IPv6 uses 128 bits. Since 128/32 = 4, an IPv6 address is four times as large in bit length.

questions.text: Identify the correct order of these major technological changes from first to fourth generation of computers. A. Transistors B. Microprocessor C. Vacuum tubes D. Integrated circuits
questions.expl: Computer generations progressed from vacuum tubes to transistors, integrated circuits, and then microprocessors. Thus the order is C, A, D, B.

questions.text: To record voice narration for a Microsoft PowerPoint presentation, a computer must have: A. Sound card B. Internet connection C. Speakers D. External video port E. Microphone
questions.expl: Voice narration requires an audio input device (microphone) and audio hardware such as a sound card. Internet access, speakers, and an external video port are not essential to recording.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II A. Blogs I. Allows users to create and edit web pages using a browser B. Podcasts II. A type of bookmarking using text labels C. Tagging III. A series of digital media files D. Wikis IV. Personal internet journals Internet terms and descriptions.
questions.expl: Blogs are personal internet journals; podcasts are series of digital media files; tagging describes content with text labels; wikis let users create and edit web pages in a browser.

questions.text: The amount of biomass produced by plants through photosynthesis minus respiration losses in a given time period is called:
questions.expl: Gross primary productivity is all photosynthetic production. After subtracting plant respiration, the remainder available for growth and consumers is net primary productivity.

questions.text: Which fuel produces the least soot particles during combustion?
questions.expl: CNG burns more cleanly than petrol, kerosene and diesel and produces substantially less particulate soot because it is a gaseous, low-carbon fuel.

questions.text: Arrange the states in ascending order of area under forest cover. A. Arunachal Pradesh B. Chhattisgarh C. Maharashtra D. Odisha E. Madhya Pradesh
questions.expl: Among these, Maharashtra has the least listed forest-cover area, followed by Odisha and Chhattisgarh; Arunachal Pradesh and then Madhya Pradesh have larger areas. The order is C, D, B, A, E.

questions.text: Eye irritation during smog is mostly caused by: A. Formaldehyde B. Peroxyacetyl nitrate C. Ozone D. Acrolein
questions.expl: Photochemical smog contains irritating oxidants and aldehydes. Peroxyacetyl nitrate, formaldehyde and acrolein are prominent lacrimators; the selected combination captures these principal eye irritants.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II A. Sendai Framework I. Equality between men and women B. Monterrey Consensus II. Our Common Future C. Beijing Declaration III. Disaster Risk Reduction D. Brundtland Report IV. Financing for development International treaties and key objectives.
questions.expl: The Sendai Framework concerns disaster-risk reduction; the Monterrey Consensus concerns financing for development; the Beijing Declaration advances gender equality; and the Brundtland Report is associated with “Our Common Future.”

questions.text: Arrange these ancient Indian institutes from east to west. A. Takshashila B. Nalanda C. Vikramshila D. Shardapeeth
questions.expl: Nalanda and Vikramshila are in Bihar, with Vikramshila east of Nalanda; Takshashila is in present-day Pakistan and Shardapeeth farther northwest in Kashmir. Hence B, C, A, D.

questions.text: Which universities were set up in 1916? A. Osmania University B. S.N.D.T. Women’s University C. Mysore University D. Patna University E. Banaras Hindu University
questions.expl: S.N.D.T. Women’s University, the University of Mysore and Banaras Hindu University were established in 1916. Osmania and Patna universities were established later.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II A. Women’s Education I. 28 B. Education of Minorities II. 21-A C. Secular Education III. 15 (Part III) D. Right to Education IV. 29 (Part III) Constitutional provisions of education and articles.
questions.expl: Article 15(3) supports special provisions for women; Article 29 protects minority interests; Article 28 concerns religious instruction in certain educational institutions; and Article 21A provides the right to education.

questions.text: Which is known as the “One Nation One Student ID” card?
questions.expl: APAAR (Automated Permanent Academic Account Registry) provides a lifelong academic identity under the “One Nation, One Student ID” initiative. Aadhaar, PAN and voter IDs identify citizens for other purposes, not their academic records.

questions.text: According to the National Credit Framework (NCrF), the credit level earned after a doctoral degree (Ph.D.) is:
questions.expl: The NCrF places the doctoral qualification at level 8, following the postgraduate level in the framework’s progression. Therefore level 7 is not the terminal doctoral level, and levels 9 and 10 are not assigned here.

The sacred journey of Lord Jagannath with brother Balabhadra and sister Subhadra from the Jagannath Temple to the divine shrine called the Gundicha Temple is known as the Car Festival or the Rath Yatra. On this occasion, the deities adorn three chariots named Nandigosha, Taladhwaja and Darpadalana respectively. They stay in the divine shrine for nine days and then return to the Jagannath Temple. This journey is called Bahuda Jatra. This grand festival of Odisha is visited by l
questions.expl: The passage identifies the Jagannath Temple and the Rath Yatra tradition with Puri, Odisha. The festival’s wider celebration does not change its primary association.

The sacred journey of Lord Jagannath with brother Balabhadra and sister Subhadra from the Jagannath Temple to the divine shrine called the Gundicha Temple is known as the Car Festival or the Rath Yatra. On this occasion, the deities adorn three chariots named Nandigosha, Taladhwaja and Darpadalana respectively. They stay in the divine shrine for nine days and then return to the Jagannath Temple. This journey is called Bahuda Jatra. This grand festival of Odisha is visited by lakhs of devotees from India and abroad who pull the
questions.expl: The passage explicitly names Lord Jagannath’s brother Balabhadra and sister Subhadra as the accompanying deities. Shiva and Hidimba are not named in the passage, so each alternative containing either one is excluded.

On this occasion, the deities adorn three chariots named Nandigosha, Taladhwaja and Darpadalana respectively. They stay in the divine shrine for nine days and then return to the Jagannath Temple. This journey is called Bahuda Jatra. This grand festival of Odisha is visited by lakhs of devotees from India and abroa

questions.expl: The passage calls the return journey after the nine-day stay Bahuda Jatra. Rath Yatra refers to the wider car-festival journey.

questions.text: Consider the grammar: S → A A → $B$ | id B → B, A | A If I₀ = CLOSURE({[S → .A]}), how many items are in GOTO(I₀, $)?
questions.expl: GOTO(I₀, $) begins with A → $.B. Its closure adds B → .B, A, B → .A, A → .$B$, and A → .id, giving five items in total. Therefore option C is correct.

questions.text: In a schema R(A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H), each field of R contains only atomic values. F= {CH→G, A →BC, B→CFH, E→A, F→EG} is a set of functional dependencies F+ is exactly the set of FDs that holds R. The relation R is :
options: In 2 NF , but not in 3 NF
questions.expl: D appears on no right-hand side, so every candidate key must contain it; taking closures gives AD, BD, ED and FD as the candidate keys. The prime attributes are therefore A, B, D, E and F, and the non-prime ones are C, G and H. But A → BC makes the non-prime attribute C depend on A alone, a proper subset of the key AD. That partial dependency breaks 2NF, while the relation is already in 1NF because every field is ato

questions.text: Which of the following statements about pointers in C are TRUE. A. Pointers can be used to access array elements B. Pointers can store the address of another pointer C. Pointers are automatically dereferenced in expression D. Pointers cannot be used to access structure members
questions.expl: (A) is true: array elements are reachable through pointer arithmetic such as *(arr + i). (B) is true: a pointer is itself a variable with an address, so a pointer to a pointer is legal. (C) is false — dereferencing is explicit, through the * operator. (D) is false — structure members are reachable with p->member. Only (A) and (B) hold, so option B is correct.

questions.text: In a token ring network the transmission speed is 10⁷ bps and the propagation speed is 200 m/μs. The 1-bit delay in this network is equivalent to ________________
questions.expl: The transmission speed is 10⁷ bps, so one bit occupies 1/10⁷ s = 0.1 μs on the wire. In that time the signal advances 0.1 μs × 200 m/μs = 20 m. The 1-bit delay is therefore equivalent to 20 metres of cable, so option A is correct.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are TRUE about mutual exclusion in concurrent programming ? A. Mutual exclusion ensures that only one process can be in a critical section at any given time. B. Mutual exclusion are designed to prevent conflicts and ensure that only one process can access shared resources at a time. C. Mutual exclusion can use various algorithms to ensure that processes do not enter the critical section simultaneously. D. Mutual exclusion allows multiple processes to access the critical section simultaneously to improve performance.
questions.expl: Statements (A), (B) and (C) all restate the same guarantee — at most one process inside the critical section at a time, enforced by locks or algorithms such as Peterson’s. (D) contradicts the definition outright, since allowing simultaneous access is exactly what mutual exclusion prevents. Only (A), (B) and (C), so option A is correct.

questions.text: Consider the function in C code : Cal(a, b) { if( b!=1 ) { if( a!=1 ) { printf("*"); Cal(a/2,b); } else { b=b-1; Cal(10,b); } } } How many times * is going to be printed, if the function is called with Cal(10, 10); ?
questions.expl: Each pass halves a by integer division, 10 → 5 → 2 → 1, printing * on the three calls where a ≠ 1. Reaching a = 1 decrements b and restarts with a = 10. That cycle runs for b = 10 down to b = 2, so nine times, giving 9 × 3 = 27 stars. Option D is correct.

A relation on {1, 2, 3, 4} is reflexive only if it contains all four self-pairs (1,1), (2,2), (3,3) and (4,4). R₁ omits (3,3); R₂ omits (2,2), (3,3) and (4,4); R₄ contains no self-pair at all. R₃ and R₅ each contain all four, so only (C) and (E) are reflexive — option D.

questions.text: Consider a relation schema R=(U, V, W, X, Y, Z), on which the following functional dependencies hold {U→V, VW→X, Y→W; X→U} The candidate keys of R are :
questions.expl: Z appears on no right-hand side, so it must belong to every candidate key. Taking closures, UY⁺ gains V from U → V, W from Y → W and X from VW → X; VY⁺ and XY⁺ reach the same set. Each covers everything except Z, so appending Z gives the candidate keys UYZ, VYZ and XYZ. Option D is correct.

questions.text: Which of the following is correct way to declare a functional pointer in C ?
questions.expl: In int ( func)(int, int); the parentheses bind * to func first, so func is a pointer to a function taking two ints and returning int. Option A declares a function returning int , and options C and D place the asterisk where the syntax does not allow it. Option B is correct.

questions.text: Arrange the following steps of Feature Drive Development (FDD) process in the correct sequence : A. Develop an overall model B. Build by feature C. Plan by feature D. Design by feature E. Build a feature list
questions.expl: Feature Driven Development runs: develop an overall model (A), build a feature list (E), plan by feature (C), design by feature (D), then build by feature (B). The model and the feature list must both exist before planning, and design always precedes build. That order is option B.

questions.text: Consider the given number (45) y where y is the base of the number. Some of the possible values of y are given below. A. 5 B. 6 C. 7 D. 8
questions.expl: In base y every digit used must be smaller than y. The numeral 45 uses the digit 5, so y must exceed 5. Base 5 is therefore invalid, while bases 6, 7 and 8 all admit the digits 4 and 5. The valid values are (B), (C) and (D) — option B.

questions.text: Consider the following C program : #include<stdio.h> int main() { int x[] = {2,4,6,8,10}; int a, b=0, *y=x+4; for( a=0; a<5; a++) { b = b +(*y-a) - *(y-a); } printf("%d\n",b); return 0; } What will be the output of the above C program ?
questions.expl: y points at x[4] = 10, and *y stays 10 throughout. Each iteration adds (10 − a) − x[4−a]: for a = 0 to 4 that is 10−10 = 0, 9−8 = 1, 8−6 = 2, 7−4 = 3 and 6−2 = 4. The running total is 0+1+2+3+4 = 10, so the program prints 10 — option D.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II (A) The activation function (I) is called the delta rule. (B) The learning method of perceptron (II) is one of the key components of the perceptron, as in the most common neural network architecture. (C) Areas of application of artificial neural networks (III) is always boolean, like a switch. (D) The output of the perceptron (IV) system identification and control.
questions.expl: The activation function is one of the key components of a perceptron, so (A)-(II). A perceptron learns by the delta rule, giving (B)-(I). Artificial neural networks are applied to tasks such as system identification and control, so (C)-(IV). A perceptron emits a boolean, switch-like output, so (D)-(III). Only option C carries all four pairings.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II (A) Representation of bits (I) Transport layer (B) Physical Address (II) Physical layer (C) Logical Address (III) Network layer (D) Segmentation and reassembly (IV) Data link layer
questions.expl: Bits are represented on the medium at the physical layer, so (A)-(II). Physical (MAC) addressing belongs to the data-link layer, giving (B)-(IV). Logical (IP) addressing belongs to the network layer, so (C)-(III). Segmentation and reassembly is a transport-layer duty, so (D)-(I). Option B matches all four.

questions.text: Which of the following are Agile Process Models ? A. Extreme Programming (XP) B. Waterfall C. Scrum D. Spiral E. Incremental
questions.expl: Extreme Programming and Scrum are both Agile methods, built on short iterations and continuous customer feedback. Waterfall is strictly sequential; Spiral is risk-driven and iterative but not Agile; the Incremental model predates the Agile movement. Only (A) and (C) qualify, so option A is correct.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are TRUE about Privileged Instructions ? A. It can only be executed by the Operating System kernel and not by user applications. B. It is designed to perform operations that can directly affect the hardware or system state such as I/O operations or changing memory management setting. C. User applications can execute privileged instructions if they have to correct permissions, set by the Operating System. D. It usually executed in user mode to ensure the safety and security of the system.
questions.expl: (A) is true — privileged instructions execute only in kernel (supervisor) mode. (B) is true — they cover exactly the operations touching hardware or system state, such as I/O and memory-management setup. (C) is false: no permission setting lets a user-mode application execute one directly; it must trap into the kernel. (D) is false: they run in kernel mode, not user mode. Only (A) and (B) — option A.

questions.text: Consider a CSMA/CD network that transmits data at the rate of 100 Mbps over a 1 Kilometre cable with no repeater. If the minimum frame size required for this network is 1250 bytes, what is the signal speed (km/sec) in the cable.
questions.expl: The minimum frame of 1250 bytes is 10,000 bits, which at 100 Mbps takes 10,000/10⁸ = 10⁻⁴ s to transmit. Collision detection requires that time to cover the round trip of 2 × 1 km. The signal speed is therefore 2 km / 10⁻⁴ s = 20,000 km/s — option D.

questions.text: Consider the Grammar: T → Qx Q → RS R → y ∣ ϵ S → z ∣ ϵ Here x, y, z are terminals and T, Q, R, S are non- terminals. What will be the follow set of the non-terminal R?
questions.expl: In Q → RS, whatever can begin S follows R, contributing z. Because S can also derive ε, anything following Q follows R as well, and T → Qx supplies x. Hence FOLLOW(R) = {z, x}, which is option C.

questions.text: Host A (on TCP/IPv4 Networks) send an IP Datagram D to host B (also on TCP/IPv4 network). Assume that no error occurred during transmission of D, when D reaches B. Which of following header field may differ from that of original datagram D ? A. TTL B. Checksum C. Fragment offset D. Source IP E. Destination IP
questions.expl: TTL is decremented by every router, so (A) changes. The header checksum covers TTL and must be recomputed at each hop, so (B) changes. Fragment offset changes whenever the datagram is fragmented in transit, so (C) may differ. Source and destination IP are never rewritten by ordinary routing, so (D) and (E) stay fixed. Only (A), (B) and (C) — option B.

questions.text: Which of the following properties correctly describe a Regular Grammar ? A. All production rules are of the form A→xB or A→x, where A and B are non terminal symbols and x is a terminal symbol. B. Regular grammars are more powerful than context-free grammars and can express any type of language. C. There is a direct correspondence between regular grammar and finite automata. D. Regular grammars can generate languages that are not recognised by any type of automata.
questions.expl: (A) is true: right-linear rules of the form A → xB or A → x define a regular grammar. (C) is true: every regular grammar has an equivalent finite automaton and vice versa. (B) is false — regular grammars are strictly weaker than context-free ones. (D) is false — the languages they generate are exactly those finite automata accept. Only (A) and (C), so option D.

questions.text: Consider a schema R(P, Q, R, S) and the following functional dependencies P → Q, Q → R, R → S, S → Q. Then decomposition of R (P, Q), R (Q, R) and R 3(Q, S) is :
options: Lossless Join but not dependency preserving
Dependency preserving but not lossless Join
Not dependency preserving and not lossless join
questions.expl: The sub-relations share Q, and Q determines R and, through R → S, also S, so rejoining them reconstructs R without spurious tuples: the decomposition is lossless. P → Q survives in R₁(P, Q), Q → R in R₂(Q, R), and R → S together with S → Q is recoverable from R₂ and R₃(Q, S). Every dependency remains enforceable, so the decomposition is both dependency preserving and lossless — option A.

questions.text: Arrange the following phases of the Agile process in the correct sequence : A. Design B. Release C. Testing D. Development E. Planning
questions.expl: Even inside a short iteration the work still flows planning (E) → design (A) → development (D) → testing (C) → release (B). Requirements are agreed before design, code precedes its tests, and release comes last. That order is option C.

questions.text: Which of the following are TRUE about constructors in C++ ? A. A constructor can be overloaded. B. A constructor does not have a return type. C. A constructor must be declared as a friend function. D. A constructor is called when an object is destroyed.
questions.expl: (A) is true — constructors can be overloaded on their parameter lists. (B) is true — a constructor has no return type, not even void. (C) is false: a constructor is an ordinary member function and is never required to be a friend. (D) is false: destruction invokes the destructor, not the constructor. Only (A) and (B), so option D.

questions.text: Let P be "It is hot day" and q be "The temperature is 48°C". Write in simple sentences the meaning of ¬p∧¬q.
options: It is hot day or temperature is 48°C
It is cold day or temperature is 48°C
It is neither a hot day nor temperature is 48°C
It is not a hot day
questions.expl: ¬p reads “it is not a hot day” and ¬q reads “the temperature is not 48°C”. The conjunction asserts both at once, which in plain English is “it is neither a hot day nor is the temperature 48°C”. Option C says exactly that; options A and B use “or”, and option D drops the second conjunct.

questions.text: If a software project has 2000 lines of code (LOC) and the average productivity rate is 10 LOC per person-hour, how many person-hours are required to complete the project?
questions.expl: Dividing total size by the productivity rate gives 2000 LOC ÷ 10 LOC per person-hour = 200 person-hours. Option C is correct.

questions.text: Arrange the following steps in proper sequence involved in a Genetic Algorithm : A. Selection B. Initialization C. Crossover D. Mutation E. Evaluation
questions.expl: A genetic algorithm initialises a population (B), evaluates each individual’s fitness (E), selects parents according to that fitness (A), recombines them by crossover (C), and finally perturbs the offspring by mutation (D). Selection needs fitness scores, so evaluation must come before it. That order is option C.

questions.text: #include<stdio.h> void f1(char *x, char *y) { char *t1; t1 = x; x = y; y = t1; } void f2(char **x, char **y) { char *t1; t1 = *x; *x = *y; *y = t1; } int main() { char *a = "ONE", *b = "TWO"; f1(a, b); printf("%s %s ", a, b); f2(&a, &b); printf("%s %s", a, b); return 0; } What is the output of the program?
questions.expl: f1 receives copies of the two pointers, so swapping them inside the function leaves a and b untouched and the first printf prints ONE TWO. f2 receives the addresses of a and b, so swapping *x and *y rewrites the caller’s own pointers and the second printf prints TWO ONE. The full output is ONE TWO TWO ONE — option A.

questions.text: What is SQL primarily used for in the context of relational databases ?
options: To display data on web pages
questions.expl: SQL is the standard language for defining and manipulating relational data: creating tables, inserting, updating and deleting rows, and querying with SELECT. User interfaces, page rendering and report formatting are the work of other tools. Option B is correct.

questions.text: Which of the following C++ statements correctly declares an abstract class ?
questions.expl: A C++ class is abstract when it declares at least one pure virtual function, written virtual void show() = 0;. Option B omits virtual, so = 0 is not valid there; option C defines an ordinary member; option D has neither a return type nor virtual. Option A is correct.

questions.text: Arrange the following recurrence relations in increasing order of their time complexity: A. T(n) = T(n/2) + 1 B. T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n C. T(n) = 3T(n/3) + n D. T(n) = 2T(n/2) + √n E. T(n) = T(n−1) + 1 Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.expl: Solving each relation: (A) T(n/2)+1 is Θ(log n); (E) T(n−1)+1 is Θ(n); (D) 2T(n/2)+√n is Θ(n); (B) 2T(n/2)+n is Θ(n log n); and (C) 3T(n/3)+n is also Θ(n log n). Ordering log n < n < n log n gives (A), (E), (D), (B), (C) — option B.

questions.text: How does a relational database ensure data integrity ?
options: By enforcing rules defined in the schema
By compressing data for efficient storage
By allowing unrestricted access to all users
questions.expl: Relational databases protect integrity through schema-level constraints — primary keys, foreign keys, unique, not-null and check constraints — which the engine enforces on every write. Encryption protects confidentiality, compression saves space, and unrestricted access would weaken integrity rather than ensure it. Option B is correct.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (IP Address) List-II (Class) (A) 10.20.30.40 (I) Class E (B) 210.20.30.3 (II) Class B (C) 180.30.100.10 (III) Class A (D) 252.5.15.11 (IV) Class C
questions.expl: The first octet fixes the class. 10 falls in 1-126, so 10.20.30.40 is Class A and (A)-(III). 210 falls in 192-223, so 210.20.30.3 is Class C and (B)-(IV). 180 falls in 128-191, so 180.30.100.10 is Class B and (C)-(II). 252 falls in 240-255, so 252.5.15.11 is Class E and (D)-(I). Option D is correct.

questions.text: Find the correct sequence of the storage devices in descending order based on their access time. A. Registers B. Magnetic Disk C. Magnetic Tapes D. Main memory E. Optical Disk
questions.expl: Descending access time means slowest first: magnetic tape (seconds), then optical disk, then magnetic disk (milliseconds), then main memory (nanoseconds), and finally registers, which are fastest. That is (C), (E), (B), (D), (A) — option D.

questions.text: A graph G with number of vertices greater and equal than three i.e. (n ≥ 3) is a Hamiltonian graph, if the degree of each vertex is greater and equal to . . . .
options: Four times of number of vertices
questions.expl: Dirac’s theorem states that a simple graph on n ≥ 3 vertices in which every vertex has degree at least n/2 is Hamiltonian. The threshold is therefore half the number of vertices, so option C is correct.

questions.text: Fifth normal form is concerned with :
questions.expl: Fifth normal form, also called project-join normal form, is concerned with join dependency: a relation is in 5NF when it cannot be decomposed further without losing information. Multivalued dependency belongs to 4NF, and functional dependency to 2NF, 3NF and BCNF. Option A is correct.

questions.text: Consider the transactions T₁, T₂, T₃, and the schedules S₁ and S₂ given below. T₁: r₁(X); r₁(Z); w₁(X); w₁(Z) T₂: r₂(Y); r₂(Z); w₂(Z) T₃: r₃(Y); r₃(X); w₃(Y) S₁: r₁(X); r₃(Y); r₃(X); r₂(Y); r₂(Z); w₃(Y); w₂(Z); r₁(Z); w₁(X); w₁(Z) S₂: r₁(X); r₃(Y); r₂(Y); r₃(X); r₁(Z); r₂(Z); w₃(Y); w₁(X); w₂(Z); w₁(Z) Which one of the following statements about the schedules is TRUE?
options: Both S₁ and S₂ are conflict-serializable
Neither S₁ nor S₂ is conflict-serializable
questions.expl: To determine conflict serializability, construct the precedence (serialization) graph for each schedule by identifying conflicting operations (different transactions accessing the same variable with at least one write): For Schedule S₁: On X : r₃(X) precedes w₁(X) → T₃ → T₁ On Y : r₂(Y) precedes w₃(Y) → T₂ → T₃ On Z : r₂(Z) and w₂(Z) precede r₁(Z) and w₁(Z) → T₂ → T₁ Edges in S₁: T₂ → T₃ → T₁ and T₂ → T₁ . questions.text: A CPU has a 5-stage pipeline with the following stages Fetch (F), Decode (D), Execute (E), Memory (M) and Write-back (W). Each stage takes one clock cycle to complete. Assume there are no pipeline stalls and the pipeline is initially empty. How many clock cycles are required to complete the execution of 10 instructions?
questions.expl: A k-stage pipeline completes n instructions in k + n − 1 cycles once it has been filled. With k = 5 and n = 10 that is 5 + 10 − 1 = 14 cycles, so option B is correct.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (computing systems) List-II (working/output) (A) Half Adder (I) Has n input and 2ⁿ output (B) Decoder (II) CPU Storage Unit (C) Register (III) Used to store program at runtime (D) Main memory (IV) 2-bit addition circuit
questions.expl: A half adder adds two bits, so (A)-(IV). A decoder turns n inputs into 2ⁿ outputs, giving (B)-(I). A register is storage inside the CPU, so (C)-(II). Main memory holds the program while it runs, so (D)-(III). Option C is correct.

questions.text: Arrange the following steps in a proper sequence for the process of training a neural network. A. Weight initialization B. Feed forward C. Back Propagation D. Loss Calculation E. Weight Update
questions.expl: Training runs: initialise the weights (A), feed the input forward to obtain predictions (B), compute the loss against the targets (D), back-propagate the gradients (C), then update the weights (E). The loss must exist before gradients can be taken, so (D) precedes (C). That order is option A.

questions.text: Consider the following statements regarding combinational and sequential circuits. A. Output of combinational circuits depends on the only current input. B. Output of combinational circuit depends on the both current input and previous output. C. Output of sequential circuit depends on the current input. D. Output of sequential circuit depends on both current input and previous output.
questions.expl: A combinational circuit’s output is a pure function of its present inputs, which makes (A) true and (B) false. A sequential circuit adds memory, so its output depends on both the present input and the stored previous state, making (D) true and (C) false. Only (A) and (D) — option B.

questions.text: Which of the following relations can not be decomposed in to BCNF with a lossless join and dependency-preserving decomposition?
questions.expl: For R(V, W, X, Y, Z) with {VW→X, WX→V, VX→W, W→Y, Y→Z}, the closure of VW reaches every attribute, so VW is a candidate key. But W → Y and Y → Z both have non-superkey left-hand sides, violating BCNF. Any decomposition that removes them separates W from Y or Y from Z, and the lost dependency cannot be re-derived from the fragments. This relation therefore admits no lossless, dependency-preserving BCNF decomposition —

questions.text: #include<iostream.h> using namespace std; void swap(int &x, int &y) { int temp=x; x=y; y=temp; } int main() { int a=5, b=10; swap(a,b); swap(a,b); cout<<a<<" "<<b; return 0; } What will be the output of the above code?
questions.expl: swap takes its parameters by reference, so the first call genuinely exchanges a and b, giving a = 10 and b = 5. The second call exchanges them straight back, restoring a = 5 and b = 10. The program prints 5 10, so option A is correct.

questions.text: Which of the following are typical activities in the software process lifecycle? A. Requirement Analysis B. System Design C. Code Refactoring D. Deployment E. Substructure
questions.expl: Requirement analysis (A), system design (B) and deployment (D) are standard phases of the software process lifecycle. Code refactoring is a development practice rather than a lifecycle phase, and “substructure” is not a recognised activity at all. Only (A), (B) and (D) — option C.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the structure of a relational database ?
options: Data organized into tables with rows and columns
Data organized into files and folders
Data organized into a hierarchical tree structure
Data organized into a network of interconnected nodes
questions.expl: A relational database stores data in tables of rows and columns, where a row is a record and a column an attribute, with relationships expressed through keys. Files and folders, tree hierarchies and node networks describe other data models. Option A is correct.

questions.text: A coin is tossed successively three times. Find the Probability (P), Event (E), Sample space (S) of getting exactly one head or two heads, where n is number of occurrence. A. n(S) = 8 and n(E) = 4 B. n(E) = 6 and n(S) = 8 C. P(E) = 3/4 D. P(E) = 1/2
questions.expl: Three tosses give n(S) = 2³ = 8. “Exactly one head or exactly two heads” covers every outcome except HHH and TTT, so n(E) = 6 and P(E) = 6/8 = 3/4. Statements (B) and (C) hold while (A) and (D) do not, so option B is correct.

questions.text: Out of the following steps in the proper sequence for simplifying a Boolean function using a Karnaugh map (K-map). A. Identify and group the largest possible cluster of 1's B. Draw the K-map for the given Boolean function C. Write the simplified Boolean expression from the grouped clusters D. Transfer the truth table values to the K-map
questions.expl: Simplifying with a Karnaugh map goes: draw the map for the function (B), transfer the truth-table values into its cells (D), group the largest possible clusters of 1s (A), then read the simplified expression off those groups (C). That order is option A.

questions.text: Consider the following, where p and q are two statements. A. ¬(p ∧ q) ≡ ¬p ∨ ¬q B. ¬(p ∨ q) ≡ ¬p ∧ ¬q C. p ∧ ¬p ≡ T D. ¬(p ⇒ q) ≡ p ∧ ¬q E. p ∨ q ≡ ¬p ∨ ¬q
questions.expl: By De Morgan’s laws ¬(p ∧ q) ≡ ¬p ∨ ¬q and ¬(p ∨ q) ≡ ¬p ∧ ¬q, so (A) and (B) hold. For (D), p ⇒ q is ¬p ∨ q, so ¬(p ⇒ q) ≡ ¬(¬p ∨ q) ≡ p ∧ ¬q — also true. (C) fails because p ∧ ¬p is a contradiction, not a tautology, and (E) fails on the row p = q = T. Only (A), (B) and (D) — option A.

questions.text: What is the output of the code given below : #include<iostream.h> using namespace std; class Base { public: Base(){ cout<<"Base Const"; } virtual ~Base() { cout<<"Base dest"; } }; class Derived : public Base { public: Derived() { cout<<"Derived Const"; } ~Derived() { cout<<"Derived dest"; } }; int main() { Base *b = new Derived(); delete b; return 0; }
options: Base Const Derived Const Derived dest Base dest
Base Const Derived Const Base dest Derived dest
Derived Const Base Const Base dest Derived dest
Base Const Derived Const Base dest
questions.expl: Constructing a Derived object runs the Base constructor first and then the Derived one, printing Base Const Derived Const. Because ~Base is declared virtual, deleting through the Base* dispatches to ~Derived first and then ~Base, printing Derived dest Base dest. The full output is option A.

questions.text: If L₁ and L₂ are context free languages, which one of the following is true about L₁ ∩ L₂?
questions.expl: Context-free languages are not closed under intersection, so L₁ ∩ L₂ need not be context-free, and it certainly need not be regular. Both languages are recursive and therefore recursively enumerable, and that class is closed under intersection, so the intersection is guaranteed to be recursively enumerable. Option C is the only statement that always holds.

questions.text: Consider the following C code: #include<stdio.h> int temp =0; int fun(int x, int y) { int z; temp++; if(y==3) return (x*x*x); else { z=fun(x,y/3); return (z*z*z); } } int main() { fun(4,81); printf("%d",temp); } what will be the output of the following code :
questions.expl: fun increments temp on entry and then recurses with y/3 until y reaches 3. The calls use y = 81, 27, 9 and 3, so temp is incremented four times including the base case, leaving temp = 4. Option B is correct.

questions.text: Which of the following tasks could be attained using syntax trees in compiler design ? A. Type Checking B. Code Generation C. Code Optimization D. Error Handling
questions.expl: A syntax tree is the structured representation the compiler walks for type checking (A), code generation (B) and code optimisation (C). It can reveal that an error exists, but recovering from errors is the job of the error-handling machinery rather than the tree itself. Only (A), (B) and (C) — option A.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II (A) HTML (I) Allow for dynamic and interactive web pages. (B) DHTML (II) Defines the structure of web pages. (C) XML (III) Object-oriented programming language for web applications. (D) JAVA (IV) Used for data storage and transport.
questions.expl: HTML defines page structure, so (A)-(II). DHTML adds dynamic, interactive behaviour, giving (B)-(I). XML carries and stores data, so (C)-(IV). Java is the object-oriented language used for web applications, so (D)-(III). Option C is correct.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Counter) List-II (uses/working) (A) N-bit Ring Counter (I) Uses universal clock (B) Synchronous Counter (II) Counts exactly N states (C) Asynchronous Counter (III) Counts 0 to 9 (D) Decimal Counter (IV) Main clock is applied to first flip-flop only
questions.expl: An N-bit ring counter cycles through exactly N states, so (A)-(II). A synchronous counter clocks every flip-flop from one common clock, giving (B)-(I). In an asynchronous (ripple) counter only the first flip-flop sees the main clock, so (C)-(IV). A decimal counter counts 0 to 9, so (D)-(III). Option C is correct.

questions.text: Arrange the following steps of file handling in C in the correct order : A. Close the file B. Read from or write to the file C. Open the file D. Check for error
questions.expl: File handling in C runs: open the file (C), check that the open succeeded (D), read from or write to it (B), then close it (A). Checking for error immediately after opening is what makes the subsequent I/O safe. That order is option C.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Algorithms) List-II (Characteristics) (A) First Come First Served (FCFS) (I) Each process is assigned a priority. (B) Shortest Job First (SJF) (II) Ensures fair allocation of CPU time by assigning time slice. (C) Round Robin (RR) (III) Processes are executed in the order they arrive. (D) Priority Scheduling (IV) Select the process for execution with smallest next Burst time.
questions.expl: FCFS runs processes in arrival order, so (A)-(III). SJF picks the process with the smallest next CPU burst, giving (B)-(IV). Round Robin shares the CPU fairly through time slices, so (C)-(II). Priority scheduling assigns each process a priority, so (D)-(I). Option C is correct.

questions.text: Arrange the following steps in a proper sequence for the typical process of a DNS query : A. Query authoritative DNS Server B. Query local DNS Server C. Local DNS Server Check Cache D. Query root DNS Server E. Query TLD DNS Server
questions.expl: Resolution starts at the local recursive resolver (B), which first checks its cache (C). On a miss it queries a root server (D), which refers it to the TLD server (E), which in turn refers it to the authoritative server (A) holding the record. That order is option D.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (operating system concepts) List-II (characteristics) (A) Paging (I) Evicts least recently used process (B) LRU (Least Recently Used) (II) Extends physical memory (C) C-SCAN (III) Logical to physical mapping (D) Virtual Memory (IV) Circular disk access
questions.expl: Paging maps logical addresses onto physical frames, so (A)-(III). LRU evicts the least recently used entry, giving (B)-(I). C-SCAN sweeps the disk in one circular direction, so (C)-(IV). Virtual memory makes the address space appear larger than physical memory, so (D)-(II). Option B is correct.

questions.text: A class B network on the Internet has a subnet mask of 255.255.248.0, what is the maximum number of hosts per subnet?
questions.expl: The mask 255.255.248.0 is 11111111.11111111.11111000.00000000, leaving 11 zero bits for the host field. That gives 2¹¹ = 2048 addresses per subnet, less the network and broadcast addresses, so 2046 usable hosts — option C.

questions.text: Select the Sorting Algorithms that are stable. A. Quick Sort B. Bubble Sort C. Insertion Sort D. Merge Sort E. Shell Sort
questions.expl: A sort is stable when records with equal keys keep their input order. Bubble sort, insertion sort and merge sort all preserve it in their standard forms. Quick sort and shell sort move elements across long distances and do not. Only (B), (C) and (D) — option D.

questions.text: ___________is a Self Balancing binary search tree, where the path from the root to the furthest leaf is no more than twice as long as the path from the root to nearest leaf.
questions.expl: A red-black tree is the self-balancing binary search tree whose colouring rules guarantee that the longest root-to-leaf path is at most twice the shortest, keeping search, insertion and deletion at O(log n). Expression, game and threaded trees carry no such balance guarantee. Option C is correct.

questions.text: Let L (x , y) be the statement "x loves y" where the domain for both x and y consists of all people in the world. Use quantifiers to express "Joy is loved by everyone".
questions.expl: “Joy is loved by everyone” says that for every person x, x loves Joy — that is ∀x L(x, Joy). Option B reverses the roles and says Joy loves everyone; option C only asserts that somebody is universally loved; option D is an existential negation. Option A is correct.

questions.text: What will be the output of the following C code? #include<stdio.h> void main() { int arr[5] = {10,20,30,40,50}; int *p = (int*) (&arr +1); printf("%d%d", *(arr+1), *(p-1)); }
questions.expl: (arr+1) is arr[1] = 20. Because &arr has type int( )[5], &arr + 1 steps a whole array forward, so p points just past arr[4]; p − 1 therefore points at arr[4] = 50. The program prints 20 50, so option B is correct.

questions.text: Arrange the following stages of a Turing Machine (TM) operation in the correct order as they occur during computation. A. Writing a symbol on the tape B. Moving the tape head left to right C. Reading a symbol from the tape D. Transitioning to a new state based on the current state and symbol read E. Halting and accepting or rejecting the input
questions.expl: One Turing machine step reads the symbol under the head (C), combines it with the current state to choose a transition (D), writes a symbol (A) and moves the head (B). The machine halts and accepts or rejects when no further transition applies (E). That order is option C.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (software design principles) List-II (Definition) (A) Cohesion (I) Degree to which one module relies on another module. (B) Coupling (II) Dividing a software system into distinct modules. (C) Abstraction (III) Degree to which elements of a module belong together. (D) Modularity (IV) Simplifying complex reality by modeling classes appropriate to the problem.
questions.expl: Cohesion measures how well the elements inside a single module belong together, so (A)-(III). Coupling measures how much one module depends on another, giving (B)-(I). Abstraction simplifies reality by modelling only the classes that matter, so (C)-(IV). Modularity is the division of the system into distinct modules, so (D)-(II). Option C is correct.

questions.text: Which of the following languages can be recognized by a Non-Deterministic Finite Automaton (NFA) but cannot be recognized by a Deterministic Finite Automaton (DFA)? A. L₁ = {w ∈ {0,1}* | the length of w is even} B. L₂ = {w ∈ {0,1}* | the length of w is odd} C. L₃ = {w ∈ {0,1}* | all 0s precede all 1s in w} D. L₄ = {w ∈ {0,1}* | w contains an equal number of 0s and 1s} E. L₅ = {w ∈ {0,1}* | all 1s precede all 0s in w}
questions.expl: NFAs and DFAs recognize exactly the same regular languages. L₁, L₂, L₃, and L₅ are regular and recognized by both, while L₄ is non-regular and recognized by neither. Therefore option D is correct.

questions.text: Given a project with an estimated effort of 1500 person-hours and a team of 5 people, how many days will it take to complete the project, if each person works 8 hours a day?
questions.expl: Five people working eight hours a day supply 40 person-hours per day. Dividing 1500 person-hours by 40 gives 37.5 days, so option B is correct.

questions.text: Arrange the following phases of database design in the correct order : A. Physical Design B. Conceptual Design C. Logical Design D. Requirement Analysis
questions.expl: Database design proceeds: requirement analysis (D), conceptual design (B) producing an ER model, logical design (C) mapping that model to relations, then physical design (A) choosing storage structures and indexes. That order is option C.

questions.text: Consider the three way hand shaking process followed during TCP connection establishment between two hosts A and B . Let S and R be two random 32 -bit starting sequence numbers chosen by A and B, respectively. Suppose A sends a TCP segment having SYN bit =1, SEQ number = S and ACK bit =0 and B accepts the connection request. Which one of the following choices represents the information present in the TCP segment header that is sent by B to A ?
options: SYN bit =1, SEQ number =S+1, ACK bit =0, ACK number =R, FiN bit =0
SYN bit =0, SEQ number =R, ACK bit =1, ACK number =S+1, FiN bit =0
SYN bit =1, SEQ number =R, ACK bit =1, ACK number =S+1, FiN bit =0
SYN bit =1, SEQ number = R, ACK bit =1, ACK number =S, FiN bit =0
questions.expl: B’s reply is a SYN-ACK. It carries B’s own initial sequence number R, sets SYN = 1 because B is opening its own direction of the connection, sets ACK = 1, and acknowledges A’s stream with ACK number S + 1. FIN stays 0. Option C matches all five fields.

questions.text: Two computers A and B are configured as follows : A has IP address 203.197.2.53 and subnet mask 255.255.128.0, B has IP address 203.197.75.201 and subnet mask 255.255.192.0. What one of the following statement is true?
options: A and B both assume they are on the same network
B assumes, A is on same network, A assumes B is on different network
A assumes, B is on same network, but B assumes, A is on a different network
A and B both assume they are on different network
questions.expl: A applies its own mask to both addresses: 203.197.2.53 and 203.197.75.201 both reduce to 203.197.0.0, so A concludes B is local. B applies its own mask: its address reduces to 203.197.64.0 but A’s reduces to 203.197.0.0, so B concludes A is remote. Option C describes exactly this asymmetry.

questions.text: In Software configuration management, what is the primary purpose of version control ?
options: To control the changes made to software
questions.expl: Within software configuration management, version control exists to record and govern changes to software artefacts over time — tracking history, enabling rollback, and supporting branching and merging. Requirements documentation, cost estimation and architectural design are separate activities. Option A is correct.

questions.text: Arrange the following stages of parsing in the correct order as they typically occur in the compilation process. A. Lexical Analysis B. Sematic Analysis C. Syntax Analysis D. Intermediate Code Generation E. Code Optimization
questions.expl: Compilation runs lexical analysis (A) to produce tokens, syntax analysis (C) to build the parse tree, semantic analysis (B) to check types and meaning, intermediate code generation (D), then code optimisation (E). That order is option B.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Queries) List-II (Probability) (A) A bag contains 6 white and 4 red balls. Two balls are drawn at random. What is the chance they will be the same colour? (I) 3/68 (B) In a pack of 52 cards, one card is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is either a king or a queen? (II) 14/68 (C) A bag contains 6 red, 4 white and 8 blue balls. If three balls are drawn at random, find the probability of 1 red and 2 white balls. (III) 2/13 (D) A bag contains 6 red, 4 white and 8 blue balls. If three balls are drawn at random, find the probability of 2 blue and 1 red balls. (IV) 7/15
questions.expl: There are C(10,2) = 45 equally likely pairs and C(6,2) + C(4,2) = 21 same-colour pairs, so the first probability is 21/45 = 7/15 and (A)-(IV). A pack holds 4 kings and 4 queens, so 8/52 = 2/13 and (B)-(III). From 18 balls C(18,3) = 816; one red with two white gives C(6,1)C(4,2) = 36, so 36/816 = 3/68 and (C)-(I). Two blue with one red gives C(8,2)C(6,1) = 168, so 168/816 = 14/68 and (D)-(II). Option D is correct.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II (A) Natural language processing (I) A method of training algorithm by rewarding desired behaviour and/or punishing undesired one. (B) Reinforcement learning (II) System designed to emulate the decision making abilities of a human expert. (C) Support vector machine (III) A branch of AI focused on understanding and generating human language. (D) Expert system (IV) A machine learning technique that finds the hyperplane that best separates different classes in a feature space.
questions.expl: Natural language processing is the AI branch for understanding and generating human language, so (A)-(III). Reinforcement learning trains by rewarding desired and punishing undesired behaviour, giving (B)-(I). A support vector machine finds the separating hyperplane, so (C)-(IV). An expert system emulates a human expert’s decisions, so (D)-(II). Option C is correct.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II (A) Dijkstra’s Algorithm (I) Find the shortest path between all pairs of vertices in a graph with positive or negative edge weights. (B) Floyd-Warshall Algorithm (II) Finds the shortest path in a weighted graph with non-negative edge weights. (C) Bellman-Ford Algorithm (III) Finds single-source shortest paths with possible negative weights. (D) Prim’s Algorithm (IV) Finds the Minimum Spanning Tree (MST).
questions.expl: Dijkstra’s algorithm needs non-negative edge weights, so (A)-(II). Floyd-Warshall solves all-pairs shortest paths, giving (B)-(I). Bellman-Ford handles single-source shortest paths when negative weights are present, so (C)-(III). Prim’s algorithm builds a minimum spanning tree, so (D)-(IV). Option B is correct.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are TRUE about Process Control Block (PCB) ? A. The PCB contains information about the process state, such as whether it is running, waiting or terminated B. The PCB includes the program code and data segments of the process C. The PCB stores the process's memory management information, such as page tables and segment tables D. The PCB is used to track process scheduling information and CPU registers for process execution
questions.expl: The process control block records the process state (A), its memory-management data such as page and segment tables (C), and its scheduling information together with the saved CPU registers (D). The program’s code and data segments live in the process’s address space, not in the PCB, so (B) is false. Only (A), (C) and (D) — option C.

questions.text: #include<stdio.h> void main() { int arr[ ] = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}; int *p = arr; printf("%d", *p++); printf("%d", *(p+1)); } Find the output of the above code?
questions.expl: *p++ yields the current target arr[0] = 1 and then advances p to arr[1]. The second statement evaluates *(p + 1), which is arr[2] = 3. The output is 1 followed by 3, so option B is correct.

questions.text: Arrange the following Language Classes in ascending order according to their expressive power, as defined by Chomsky hierarchy: A. Context-free languages B. Context-sensitive languages C. Regular languages D. Unrestricted Grammars
questions.expl: By expressive power the Chomsky hierarchy runs regular ⊂ context-free ⊂ context-sensitive ⊂ unrestricted, recognised respectively by finite automata, pushdown automata, linear bounded automata and Turing machines. Ascending order is therefore (C), (A), (B), (D) — option A.

questions.text: An undirected graph has vertex set V and edge set E. If it has l edges, what is the sum of the degrees of all vertices?
questions.expl: Each undirected edge contributes one to the degree of each of its two endpoints. By the handshaking lemma, the total degree is 2l, so option A is correct.

questions.text: 40 software professionals were interviewed for a job. 25 knew PYTHON 20 knew JAVA and 7 knew neither language. How many knew both languages ?
questions.expl: Seven knew neither language, so 33 of the 40 knew at least one. By inclusion-exclusion |P ∪ J| = |P| + |J| − |P ∩ J|, giving 33 = 25 + 20 − |P ∩ J|, so |P ∩ J| = 12. Option A is correct.

questions.text: A. In IPv4 addressing, a block of address can be define as x.y.z.t/ n in which x.y.z.t define one of the address and / n define the mask B. The first address in the block can be found by setting the rightmost 32-n bits to 0s C. Address of class C is used for multicast communication D. There are five classes in IPv4 address E. Supernetting combine several networks into one large network
questions.expl: (A) is true — x.y.z.t/n names a block by one address and a prefix length. (B) is true — zeroing the rightmost 32 − n bits yields the first address of the block. (D) is true — IPv4 defines classes A through E. (E) is true — supernetting aggregates contiguous blocks into one larger route. (C) is false: multicast uses class D, not class C. So (A), (B), (D) and (E) — option B.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Testing Type) List-II (Description) (A) Unit testing (I) Testing individual components of the software. (B) Integration testing (II) Testing the interaction between integrated components. (C) System testing (III) Testing to verify the system meets business needs. (D) Acceptance testing (IV) Testing the complete system to ensure it meets requirements.
questions.expl: Unit testing exercises individual components, so (A)-(I). Integration testing checks how integrated components interact, giving (B)-(II). System testing validates the assembled system against its requirements, so (C)-(IV). Acceptance testing confirms the system meets business needs, so (D)-(III). Option B is correct.

questions.text: Consider the following statement regarding special purpose registers. A. Program Counter (PC) keeps the track of next instruction executed B. Instruction register holds the address of first instruction to be executed C. Accumulator holds the output of ALU D. Program Counter ( PC ) keeps the track of only first instruction of the program
questions.expl: (A) is true — the program counter holds the address of the next instruction to be executed. (C) is true — the accumulator holds the ALU’s result. (B) is false: the instruction register holds the instruction currently being executed, not an address. (D) is false: the PC tracks the next instruction throughout execution, not only the first. Only (A) and (C) — option A.

questions.text: Arrange the following steps in the correct order to solve the Knapsack problem using Dynamic Programming. A. Define the base case when the capacity is zero (0) or no items are left to consider B. Compute the maximum value that can be obtained using items up to the i-th item and a knapsack capacity of 0 C. Identify subproblems and their dependencies based on items weights and values D. Initialize a table to store results of subproblems E. Iterate through each item and each possible Capacity to fill the table
questions.expl: The dynamic-programming solution starts from the base case of zero capacity or no items left (A), identifies the subproblems and how they depend on item weights and values (C), initialises the table that stores them (D), iterates over every item and capacity to fill it (E), and finally reads the maximum value out of the completed table (B). That order is option C.

questions.text: A multi processor system with 16 processors is used to execute a parallelizable task. If the serial portion of the task takes 200 clock cycles and the parallel portion take 800 clock cycles. When all 16 processor are used how many total clock cycles are required to complete the task ?
questions.expl: The 200-cycle serial portion cannot be sped up. The 800-cycle parallel portion divides across 16 processors, taking 800/16 = 50 cycles. The total is 200 + 50 = 250 cycles, so option A is correct.

questions.text: Arrange the given steps required for a Direct Memory Access (DMA) transfer in the correct order. A. Initiate DMA transfer request B. Transfer data directly between peripheral and memory C. Processor grants DMA control over the system bus D. DMA controller completes data transfer and signals completion
questions.expl: A DMA transfer begins with the peripheral raising a transfer request (A). The processor then releases the bus and grants the controller DMA control (C). The controller moves data directly between peripheral and memory (B), and finally signals completion (D). That order is option B.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Recurrence Relation) List-II (Complexity) (A) T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n (I) T(n) = θ(n log n) {exact solution} (B) T(n) = T(n/2) + 1 (II) O(n²) (C) T(n) = 2T(n/2) + 1 (III) T(n) = θ(n) {exact solution} (D) T(n) = T(n−1) + n (IV) O(n)

T(n) = 2T(n/2) + 1 is θ(n), and T(n) = T(n/2) + 1 is θ(log n) — which is not listed, so the official key pairs (B) with the remaining O(n)-family entry. The official NTA key is option C. questions.text: Translate ∀x ∃y (x < y) into English. Consider the domain to be the real numbers for both variables.
options: For all real numbers x, there exists a real number y such that x is less than y
For every real numbers y, there exists a real number x such that x is less than y
For some real numbers x, there exists a real number y such that x is less than y
For each and every real numbers x and y, x is less than y
questions.expl: ∀x binds every real number x, and for each of them ∃y asserts that some real y exists with x < y. Read literally: for all real numbers x there exists a real number y such that x is less than y. Option A states this; option B swaps the quantified variables, option C weakens ∀ to “for some”, and option D collapses both quantifiers into a single universal claim.

questions.text: A vector processor with 16 lanes can perform an operation on 1024 elements with each operation taking 5 clock cycles. How many cycles are needed to complete the operation?
questions.expl: With 16 lanes, 1024 elements are covered in 1024/16 = 64 passes through the vector pipeline, so option A is the official key. Note the wording: each pass is stated to take 5 clock cycles, so the number of cycles would be 64 × 5 = 320. The key counts operations rather than cycles.

questions.text: Given a project that uses the COCOMO model with an estimated effort of 2000 person-months and a productivity rate of 5 person-month per KLOC, what is the estimated size of the project in KLOC ?
questions.expl: Dividing effort by the productivity rate gives 2000 person-months ÷ 5 person-months per KLOC = 400 KLOC, so option B is correct.

questions.text: Which of the following languages are context-free? A. {wⁱxʲyᵏzˡ | i + k = j + l; i, j, k, l ≥ 0} B. {wⁱxʲyᵏzˡ | i = j and k = l; i, j, k, l ≥ 0} C. {wⁱxʲyᵏzˡ | i = j = k and k ≠ l; i, j, k, l ≥ 0} D. {wⁱxʲyᵏzˡ | i = j = k + l; i, j, k, l ≥ 0} E. {wⁱxʲyᵏzˡ | i = j = l and k ≠ l; i, j, k, l ≥ 0}
questions.expl: Language A has one balance condition that can be handled by a stack, and language B is an intersection/concatenation of simple equality constraints expressible as a context-free language. The remaining languages impose simultaneous multi-count dependencies that are not context-free, so option A is correct.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a requirement for Banker's algorithm to grant a resource request ? The Banker’s Algorithm is a critical deadlock avoidance method in operating systems, designed to facilitate resource allocation without causing deadlock. It operates by maintaining information about the maximum resources each process may require, the currently allocated resources and the available resources in the system. The algorithm checks each resource request to determine if granting it would leave the system in a safe state, meaning that there is always a sequence in which all processes can complete their execution without getting stuck due to resource unavailability. Each process must spec
options: The requested resources must be available.
The system must be in a safe state after granting the request
The request must not exceed the maximum resources the process can request.
The process must be the only one requesting resources.
questions.expl: Banker’s algorithm grants a request only when the resources are available, when the request stays within the process’s previously declared maximum, and when the resulting state is safe. It never requires a process to be the only one requesting resources — several processes hold and request concurrently. Option D is therefore the statement that is NOT a requirement.

questions.text: Which data structure does the Banker's Algorithm use to maintain the state of available, maximum and allocated resources ? The Banker’s Algorithm is a critical deadlock avoidance method in operating systems, designed to facilitate resource allocation without causing deadlock. It operates by maintaining information about the maximum resources each process may require, the currently allocated resources and the available resources in the system. The algorithm checks each resource request to determine if granting it would leave the system in a safe state, meaning that there is always a sequence in which all processes can complete their execution without getting stuck due to resource unavailabili
questions.expl: The algorithm tracks Available as a vector, and Maximum, Allocation and Need as matrices indexed by process and by resource type. Priority queues, hash tables and wait-for graphs appear elsewhere in deadlock handling but not in this algorithm. Option D is correct.

questions.text: What is the significance of the Banker's algorithm in terms of resource management? The Banker’s Algorithm is a critical deadlock avoidance method in operating systems, designed to facilitate resource allocation without causing deadlock. It operates by maintaining information about the maximum resources each process may require, the currently allocated resources and the available resources in the system. The algorithm checks each resource request to determine if granting it would leave the system in a safe state, meaning that there is always a sequence in which all processes can complete their execution without getting stuck due to resource unavailability. Each process must specify its maxim
options: It enures that all processes can finish their execution without deadlock.
It eliminates the need for processes to request resources.
It accelerates the execution of critical sections in processes.
It minimizes the number of context switches between processes.
questions.expl: Its significance is that by admitting only requests which leave the system in a safe state, it guarantees a sequence exists in which every process can run to completion — deadlock is avoided rather than merely detected afterwards. It does not remove the need to request resources, accelerate critical sections, or reduce context switches. Option A is correct.

questions.text: What is the primary goal of the Banker's Algorithm? The Banker’s Algorithm is a critical deadlock avoidance method in operating systems, designed to facilitate resource allocation without causing deadlock. It operates by maintaining information about the maximum resources each process may require, the currently allocated resources and the available resources in the system. The algorithm checks each resource request to determine if granting it would leave the system in a safe state, meaning that there is always a sequence in which all processes can complete their execution without getting stuck due to resource unavailability. Each process must specify its maximum demand for each resource type
options: To prevent processes from requesting resources
To detect and recover from deadlocks
questions.expl: Banker’s algorithm is a deadlock-avoidance method: its goal is to allocate resources in the way that keeps the system in a safe state. Option C describes deadlock detection and recovery, which is a different strategy, while options B and D describe aims the algorithm does not pursue. Option A is correct.

questions.text: What information is used to determine if a resource request can be granted ? The Banker’s Algorithm is a critical deadlock avoidance method in operating systems, designed to facilitate resource allocation without causing deadlock. It operates by maintaining information about the maximum resources each process may require, the currently allocated resources and the available resources in the system. The algorithm checks each resource request to determine if granting it would leave the system in a safe state, meaning that there is always a sequence in which all processes can complete their execution without getting stuck due to resource unavailability. Each process must specify its maximum dema
options: Available resources and current allocation of each process
Number of processes waiting for resources
questions.expl: The safety check compares the resources currently available against what each process still needs, which follows from its declared maximum and its current allocation. CPU utilisation, the length of the waiting queue and arrival times play no part in the decision. Option A is correct.
